Rust uses lines().\n       - isDisproportionateMatch:\n         - JS L683-691 applies it to every replacer and throws \"Refusing replacement because the matched span is much larger than oldString...\".\n         - Rust L504 applies it only in block anchor and silently filters, so the error becomes \"oldString not found\".\n       - Uniqueness and replacement position:\n         - JS replace (L655-713) requires the matched search string to be unique (indexOf == lastIndexOf), or uses split/join for replaceAll.\n         - Rust fuzzy replacers use `replacen(&matched, new, 1)`, which hits the first occurrence anywhere and has no uniqueness check on the matched text.\n       - Final error:\n         - JS reports \"multiple matches\" when any replacer found text present.\n         - Rust L333-343 reports \"multiple matches\" only if content contains old_string literally.\n       - EscapeNormalized: JS also handles a backslash followed by a newline; Rust does not.\n     - JS's EMPTY_OLD_STRING_ERROR is identical in both.\n   - **multiedit** (js/src/tool/multiedit.ts vs rust/src/tool/multiedit.rs): JS is unregistered and Rust is registered. With empty edits, JS throws a TypeError at results.at(-1)! (L52) while Rust returns empty output (L111). Otherwise equivalent.\n   - **write** (js/src/tool/write.ts vs rust/src/tool/write.rs)\n     - JS adds a permission check, a lock and FileTime.read (L30-53). Rust has none of these.\n     - JS relies on Bun.write to create parent directories; Rust creates them explicitly (L73-77).\n     - The BOM logic is equivalent.\n     - Descriptions differ: JS write.txt says \"MUST use the Read tool first... will fail\", which is false in JS. Rust's description says \"Will create parent directories\".\n   - **bash** (js/src/tool/bash.ts vs rust/src/tool/bash.rs)\n     - Default timeout: JS L21 uses 60 000 ms; Rust L18 uses 120 000. Both cap at 600 000.\n     - Timeout validation: JS rejects a negative timeout (L174-178) and accepts floats. Rust u64 rejects both.\n     - Shell:\n       - JS selectShell (L47-63) uses $SHELL unless it is fish or nu, falling back to zsh on darwin and bash elsewhere, or the platform shell on win32.\n       - Rust L111 always runs `bash -c`.\n     - stdin: JS uses 'ignore' (L301). Rust Command does not set stdin, so the child inherits the agent's stdin.\n     - Output:\n       - JS interleaves stdout and stderr in arrival order into one buffer (L236-260).\n       - Rust combine (L253-268) prints stdout, then \"\\n--- stderr ---\\n\", then stderr.\n     - Title: JS L377 uses the command. Rust L98-106 uses the description, or else the first 3 words.\n     - Metadata keys:\n       - JS: {output, exit, signal, timedOut, aborted, description}.\n       - Rust: {exitCode, exit, signal, output, command}, plus timedOut only on timeout.\n     - Timeout output:\n       - JS: \"Exit code unavailable (signal SIGTERM)\\n<output>\\n\\n(Command timed out after N ms)\", via processResult in js/src/tool/process-result.ts.\n       - Rust L147-157: \"Exit code unavailable\\n<output>\\n\\nCommand timed out after Nms\".\n     - Kill and abort:\n       - Rust kills only the bash child (SIGKILL); JS kills with SIGTERM and a 200 ms grace.\n       - JS supports ctx.abort and the \"(Command was aborted)\" message; Rust has no abort.\n     - Permissions: JS has tree-sitter permission checks (L187-229); Rust has none.\n     - The Rust description says \"persistent shell session\".\n     - Matching in both: tail truncation (\"...output truncated...\\n\\n\", 2000 lines / 30 000 bytes) and the non-zero \"Exit code N\\n\" prefix.\n   - **glob** (js/src/tool/glob.ts, JS side read so far)\n     - Uses Ripgrep.files with cwd=search, a glob pattern and the abort signal; the limit is 100.\n     - Results are sorted by mtime descending and printed as absolute paths.\n     - Messages: \"No files found\" when empty, and \"\\n(Results are truncated. Consider using a more specific path or pattern.)\" when cut.\n     - Metadata: {count, truncated}. Title: relative(worktree, search).\n   - **grep** (js/src/tool/grep.ts, JS side read so far)\n     - Validation and arguments:\n       - The search path resolves against Instance.directory, and a missing path throws \"Search path does not exist: X\".\n       - rg runs with --json --hidden --no-messages --no-config --glob=!**/.git/** --regexp pattern [--glob include] path.\n     - Execution: 30 s timeout with \"Search timed out after 30 seconds...\", and both pipes are drained concurrently.\n     - rg exit codes:\n       - 1 → \"No files found\".\n       - 2 with a regex parse error → \"Invalid regex pattern: ...\".\n       - Any other non-zero except 2 → \"Exit code N\\nripgrep failed\".\n       - 2 otherwise → appends \"(Some paths were inaccessible and skipped)\".\n     - Output:\n       - Results are sorted by mtime and limited to 100.\n       - The header is \"Found N matches\", then a \"path:\" line per file and \"  Line N: <focused window, 2000>\" per match, with a blank line between files.\n       - When cut it adds the truncation note.\n     - Metadata: {matches, truncated}. Before, commands ran in Node's default `/bin/sh` (dash on Debian). Now `$SHELL` is used unless it is fish or nu, so tcsh, csh, pwsh, xonsh and elvish users get a non-POSIX shell, and zsh handles globs and word-splitting differently. Fix: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_BASH_SHELL`, and only accept POSIX shells (sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh) instead of blocking two.\n2. **T6, medium: read resolves relative paths from a different base** (`read.ts:45`). It used the repo root (`Instance.worktree`); now it uses the current directory (`Instance.directory`). Run from a subdirectory, the same relative path reads a different file or fails. Fix: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_READ_RELATIVE_TO_WORKTREE`, or try both bases.\n3. **T12, medium: glob and ls no longer follow symlinked directories** (`ripgrep.ts:227-234`). `--follow` was removed, which loses results in pnpm and symlinked monorepos. `--no-config` was added, so a user's ripgrep config is now ignored. Fix: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_GLOB_FOLLOW_SYMLINKS`.\n4. **M2, medium: the MCP `timeout` setting now also limits connect and startup** (`mcp/index.ts:40-42, 322`). It is documented as the tool-listing timeout (\"Defaults to 5000\"); unset, connect gets 30 s. A small value now breaks slow `npx`/`uvx` cold starts. Fix: a separate `connect_timeout`.\n5. **S1/S2/S4/S6, medium: new error names in JSON events and storage.** `ContextOverflowError`, `RetryTimeoutExceededError`, `SocketConnectionError` and `TimeoutError` replace what used to be `APIError` or `UnknownError`.\n   - Errors that were `UnknownError` (zlib errors, rate-limit text) are now retryable `APIError`s.\n   - `APIError.message` now has the response body appended, and HTML 401/403 bodies are replaced with fixed text.\n   - Fix: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_LEGACY_ERROR_NAMES`, or put the detail in a new field and leave `message` alone.\n6. **S10, medium: `tokens.output` no longer includes reasoning tokens** (`session/index.ts:~782`). Usage numbers shift for reasoning models. Fix: `..._TOKENS_OUTPUT_INCLUDES_REASONING`, or add an `outputTotal` field.\n7. **S5, medium: a context overflow now triggers automatic compaction**, which adds LLM calls and summary messages. The existing `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT` already turns this off.\n8. **S7, medium: the agent loop keeps going after tool calls even when the finish reason is `stop`** (`prompt.ts:280, 367`). That means an extra LLM step and more cost. JS L271-276).\n     - Not-found suggestions do not appear in the Rust message.\n     - JS records FileTime.read (L246).\n     - text_window byte_offset_to_char_index differs for an offset in the middle of a character.\n   - **edit.**\n     - Missing in Rust:\n       - FileTime.assert (JS L106), i.e. the read-before-edit check.\n       - FileTime.withLock (L83).\n       - Permission.check (L69).\n     - Missing-file message:\n       - JS: \"File X not found\" (L103).\n       - Rust: FileNotFound (L126-131).\n     - Directory: JS says \"Path is a directory, not a file\" (L104-105); Rust returns the raw IO error (L133).\n     - Non-UTF-8 files fail in Rust.\n     - Line endings:\n       - JS (L19-34, L112-120) converts oldString to the file's line ending.\n       - Rust normalizes to LF and then restores endings (L142-149, L216-239).\n     - BOM: JS strips it via Bom.split/join (L107, L121-126); Rust does not.\n     - Metadata:\n       - filediff.before/after: JS keeps the original endings (L144-154); Rust uses LF (L172-181).\n       - Diff format: JS uses createTwoFilesPatch+trimDiff; Rust create_diff (L242-269) has no @@ headers.\n     - oldString==newString:\n       - JS throws a plain error (L59).\n       - Rust returns InvalidArguments (L82-87).\n     - Replacer differences:\n       - WhitespaceNormalized: JS L389-437, Rust L427-466.\n       - BlockAnchor:\n         - JS (L250-387) picks the best candidate.\n         - Rust (L469-530) returns None when there are several candidates.\n         - Blank middle lines score 1/n in Rust (L543-546).\n       - isDisproportionateMatch:\n         - JS applies it to all replacers and throws \"Refusing replacement…\" (L683-691).\n         - Rust applies it only in block anchor and silently filters (L504).\n       - Rust fuzzy replacers use replacen(&matched,…,1) with no uniqueness check; JS replace is at L655-713.\n       - Rust reports \"multiple matches\" only on a literal match (L333-343).\n       - EscapeNormalized: Rust lacks the backslash-newline case.\n   - **multiedit.**\n     - JS multiedit is unregistered; Rust's is registered.\n     - With empty edits, JS throws a TypeError at results.at(-1)! (L52); Rust returns empty output (L111).\n   - **write.**\n     - Rust lacks the permission check, lock and FileTime (JS L30-53).\n     - The JS write.txt claims \"MUST use the Read tool first\", which JS does not enforce.\n   - **bash.**\n     - Default timeout: JS 60 000 (L21), Rust 120 000 (L18).\n     - Timeout validation: JS rejects negative values (L174-178); Rust u64 rejects floats.\n     - Shell:\n       - JS selectShell uses $SHELL, excluding fish and nu (L47-63).\n       - Rust always uses `bash -c` (L111).\n     - stdin: JS uses 'ignore' (L301); Rust inherits stdin.\n     - Output:\n       - JS interleaves stdout and stderr (L236-260).\n       - Rust prints stdout, then \"\\n--- stderr ---\\n\", then stderr (combine, L253-268).\n     - Title: JS uses the command (L377); Rust uses the description or the first 3 words (L98-106).\n     - Metadata keys:\n       - JS: {output, exit, signal, timedOut, aborted, description}.\n       - Rust: {exitCode, exit, signal, output, command, [timedOut]}.\n     - Timeout text:\n       - JS: \"Exit code unavailable (signal SIGTERM)…(Command timed out after N ms)\" (process-result.ts).\n       - Rust: \"Exit code unavailable…Command timed out after Nms\" (L147-157).\n     - Kill and abort: Rust uses SIGKILL on the child only and has no abort.\n     - Rust has no tree-sitter permission (JS L187-229).\n     - The Rust description says \"persistent shell session\".\n\n   **New findings in this segment:**\n   - **glob.**\n     - Implementations:\n       - JS (js/src/tool/glob.ts): rg --files --hidden --no-config --glob=!.git/* --glob=pattern (ripgrep.ts L220-240). It has no --follow, so it does not follow symlinks, and it respects .gitignore.\n       - Rust (rust/src/tool/glob.rs L69-107) uses the `glob` crate on base.join(pattern).\n     - Pattern semantics: in rg, a pattern without a slash such as \"*.ts\" matches at any depth and braces are supported. In the glob crate, \"*.ts\" matches only the top level and braces are not supported.\n     - Rust follows symlinks (the glob crate uses metadata) and ignores .gitignore.\n     - Hidden files: Rust `*` matches dotfiles (require_literal_leading_dot false) and Rust does not exclude .git, so `**/*` would list .git files. JS excludes .git.\n     - Output:\n       - JS prints absolute paths (L52); Rust prints ctx.relative_path (L120).\n       - With no results JS prints \"No files found\" (L50); Rust prints \"\".\n     - Truncation: JS truncates after the first 100 rg results and then sorts; Rust sorts everything and keeps the top 100. The truncation message format is the same.\n     - Title: JS uses relative(worktree, search) (L62); Rust uses the pattern (L84).\n     - A nonexistent or non-directory path in JS gives \"No such file or directory: 'X'\" or \"Search path is not a directory\" (ripgrep.ts); Rust returns an empty result.\n     - An invalid pattern gives \"Invalid pattern\" in Rust.\n     - Branch: this branch added the Rust LIMIT and truncated logic (diff). The other glob divergences pre-date the branch.\n   - **grep.** The schemas are completely different.\n     - Parameters:\n       - JS (grep.ts L17-35): {pattern, path, include}.\n       - Rust (grep.rs L33-63): {pattern, path, glob, output_mode (default \"files_with_matches\"), -i, -n, -B, -A, -C, head_limit}.\n       - JS `include` is silently ignored by Rust. Rust's default output_mode lists files only, while JS lists matching lines.\n     - Search engine and walk:\n       - Rust uses its own WalkDir walker plus the regex crate; it does not shell out to rg.\n       - Rust follow_links(true) (L210) follows symlinks, while JS rg does not.\n       - Rust has no .gitignore support and skips only the `.git` name (L215-220, changed by this branch from is_hidden).\n     - Glob filter: Rust matches_glob (L243-253) supports only \"*.ext\" and \"**/*.ext\" or an exact name, with no braces.\n     - Unreadable files: Rust read_to_string silently skips non-UTF-8 files.\n     - Output format:\n       - Rust content mode: \"relpath:N: line\", with no header and no grouping.\n       - JS: \"Found N matches\\n/abs/path:\\n  Line N: …\", grouped by file, mtime-sorted, limit 100, with the truncation note.\n       - Rust has no mtime sort, no 100 limit (only head_limit) and no \"No files found\"; empty output is \"\".\n     - Metadata: JS {matches, truncated}; Rust {count}.\n     - Errors:\n       - Bad regex: JS \"Invalid regex pattern: …\"; Rust \"Invalid regex: …\", and regex-crate syntax differs from rg's.\n       - Missing path: JS \"Search path does not exist: X\"; Rust returns empty.\n       - The 30 s timeout, the exit-2 \"(Some paths were inaccessible and skipped)\" message and abort are absent in Rust.\n     - Lines and CRLF: Rust uses lines() and strips CRLF; JS uses stripTrailingLineEnding. Rust case-insensitivity is via (?i).\n     - Branch: only the hidden-file change is from this branch. The schema divergence pre-dates the branch.\n   - **list/ls** (js/src/tool/ls.ts vs rust/src/tool/list.rs).\n     - Ignore patterns:\n       - JS (L8-33) has 24 entries, with 'vendor/' duplicated, turned into rg globs `!${p}*` plus user globs `!${p}`. Real globs, .gitignore respected, hidden files included.\n       - Rust DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS (L17-41) uses exact-name matching via should_ignore (L193-208, which has a dead branch). User ignore patterns are exact names only, with no glob support and no .gitignore.\n       - Example: JS ignores \"zig-out*\" and \".coverage*\" as prefixes; Rust needs an exact name.\n     - Truncation:\n       - Rust appends \"\\n(Results are truncated. Consider using a more specific path or pattern.)\\n\" (L248-252); JS has no such note.\n       - Both set truncated when files.length >= 100 (JS L119, Rust L162-165).\n     - Errors:\n       - A missing path in Rust gives FileNotFound (L111-116); JS gives \"No such file or directory: 'X'\" from ripgrep.ts.\n       - Not a directory: Rust \"Not a directory: X\" (L118-123); JS \"Search path is not a directory: X\".\n     - Title: Rust uses relative_path or \".\" (L173-177); JS uses relative(worktree).\n     - Header line is the same: `${searchPath}/`.\n     - Order: rg traversal order vs walkdir order.\n     - Unchanged by the branch, except that JS now passes the abort signal.\n   - **webfetch** (js/src/tool/webfetch.ts vs rust/src/tool/webfetch.rs).\n     - Same in both: 5 MB limit, 30 s default and 120 s max timeout, \"markdown\" default format, the Cloudflare 403 cf-mitigated retry with UA \"agent\" (Branding.BINARY='agent'), and the title \"url (content-type)\".\n     - Differences:\n       - Permission.check: JS calls it (L46-53); Rust does not.\n       - Accept header for html: Rust (L157) lacks \"text/markdown;q=0.7\".\n       - Invalid URL: Rust returns InvalidArguments (L139-144).\n       - Status error text: Rust formats StatusCode Display, e.g. \"404 Not Found\" (L196-199); JS prints \"404\".\n       - Timeout message: Rust says \"Request timed out\"; JS says \"Request timed out after N seconds\" (L124).\n       - timeout param: Rust u64 rejects floats.\n     - Body handling:\n       - Rust reads Content-Length before the body and rejects early.\n       - Rust decodes with from_utf8_lossy.\n       - JS reads content-type after the body; Rust reads it before.\n     - extract_text_from_html (Rust L245-305): **bug**. It compares the whole tag buffer, so `<script type=\"x\">` or `<style media=…>` with attributes is NOT skipped. Rust also collapses all whitespace, while JS's HTMLRewriter (L183-208) keeps it, only trimming, and handles nested depth.\n     - html_to_markdown (Rust L308-335) is hand-rolled; JS uses Turndown (L210-220). The output differs substantially, e.g. lists, tables and blank lines are dropped.\n     - Rust remove_tag_with_content uses lowercased indices into the original string, which is a possible panic on non-ASCII.\n     - The branch changed both sides (bounded body, CF retry).\n   - **websearch** (js/src/tool/websearch.ts plus util/exa-mcp.ts vs rust/src/tool/websearch.rs).\n     - Same in both: EXA_API_KEY, a 25 s timeout, the 5 MB limit, SSE/JSON parsing, and the \"No search results found…\" text.\n     - Differences:\n       - numResults 0: JS uses `||` so it becomes 8; Rust keeps 0.\n       - Rust does not validate the livecrawl/type enums.\n       - Status text: Rust prints \"429 Too Many Requests\", JS \"429\".\n       - A malformed `data:` line throws a SyntaxError in JS but is skipped in Rust.\n       - Rust description is a different text from websearch.txt, and the year is cached in a OnceLock.\n       - Rust has no abort.\n   - **codesearch.**\n     - tokensNum out of [1000, 50000]: JS fails zod validation (L30-34); Rust clamps (L99-102).\n     - Rust descriptions differ.\n     - Otherwise equivalent: 30 s timeout, same request and messages.\n   - **batch** (js/src/tool/batch.ts vs rust/src/tool/batch.rs).\n     - Discarded calls (Rust **bug**): Rust uses `.take(MAX_BATCH_CALLS + 1)` (L118-121), so only the 11th call is reported as discarded and calls 12 and later are silently dropped. totalCalls, tools and details are wrong. Re-check of the README §4–§5 \"n/a\" Rust entries\n- **grep.** Rust uses its own WalkDir + regex walker, not rg. The rg-specific fixes (exit 2, pipe, timeout, `--no-config`) genuinely are n/a. However, the walker **follows symlinks** (`grep.rs` L211) and **ignores .gitignore**; record these as divergences, not n/a.\n- **read relative paths.** **Not n/a.** Rust resolves them via `ctx.resolve_path` (`read.rs` L115). Rust's lack of `..` normalisation differs from `path.resolve`.\n- **glob symlinks.** Rust (`glob` crate) **follows** symlinks; JS rg does not. Not n/a. Rust list uses `follow_links(false)`, which matches JS.\n- **FileTime read-before-edit.** Rust has **no** FileTime, so it has no read-before-edit check, no lock and no read stamps. CLI and JSON I/O (`js/src/index.js`, `js/src/cli/**`, `js/src/config/config.ts` ↔ `rust/src/cli.rs`)\n- **Options only in JS.**\n  - `--read-only` and `--disable-tools` (`cli/run-options.js` L216-226).\n  - Subcommands `mcp`, `auth`, `models`, `agent`, `export`, `stats` (index.js L655-661, `cli/cmd/*`).\n  - The middleware mapping `--output-format` to `json-standard` (run-options.js L144-159).\n- **Options only in Rust.** `--working-directory`.\n- **Accepted but no-op in Rust.** `--json-standard claude`, `--input-format`, and `InputMessage.tools`.\n- **Execution.** The Rust CLI **never executes tools or calls a model**. `run_with_input` prints \"Agent (Rust) ready…\" text and finishes with `step_finish{reason:\"stop\"}`.\n- **Env vars read by JS only** (`config/config.ts`, plus `.lenv` via lino-arguments): every `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` variable for\n  - VERBOSE, DRY_RUN, GENERATE_TITLE, OUTPUT_RESPONSE_MODEL, SUMMARIZE_SESSION, COMPACT_JSON\n  - CONFIG, CONFIG_DIR, CONFIG_CONTENT\n  - DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, DISABLE_PRUNE, ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_MODELS, DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT, EXPERIMENTAL, EXPERIMENTAL_WATCHER\n  - RETRY_TIMEOUT, MAX_RETRY_DELAY, MIN_RETRY_INTERVAL, STREAM_CHUNK/STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, MCP_DEFAULT/MAX_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT\n  - VERIFY_IMAGES_AT_READ_TOOL, **READ_ONLY**, **DISABLE_TOOLS**\n- **Env vars read by Rust.** Only DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_COMPACTION_MODEL(S), DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SAFETY_MARGIN_PERCENT (`defaults.rs`), and PERMISSION_MODE / PERMISSION (`permission.rs` L35-65).\n- **Events emitted by JS.** status, step_start, text, tool_use, tool_result, step_finish, error, input, init, config, idle, session_idle, log, message, permission_request, result, warning.\n  - Envelopes carry `{type, timestamp, sessionID, part}` (`cli/event-handler.js` L57-145). Utilities\n- **binary.** These are unrelated modules that share a name.\n  - JS `util/binary.ts` provides `Binary.search/insert` over sorted arrays, which has no Rust counterpart.\n  - Rust `util/binary.rs` holds binary/image detection, ported from read.ts `isBinaryFile` (L481-542), `isImageFile` (L365-390) and `validateImageFormat` (L401-452). The port is equivalent.\n- **filesystem.**\n  - **BUG:** Rust `contains` (`util/filesystem.rs` L52-65) canonicalises, which follows symlinks. When a path does not exist it falls back to a **string prefix**, so `contains(\"/a/b\",\"/a/bc\")` returns true. JS `util/filesystem.ts` uses a lexical `relative()`, which returns false.\n  - Rust `overlaps` is component-based; JS uses string `startsWith('..')`.\n  - Rust lacks `up`/`globUp` (JS L29-72).\n  - The Rust `Filesystem` module is unused.\n- **id.**\n  - Same format and algorithm, and Rust adds `Prefix::Call`.\n  - Rust panics where JS throws; for example, given `\"\"` JS generates a new id while Rust panics.\n  - Rust's counter does a non-atomic load-then-store.\n  - JS `randomBase62` is modulo-biased (`byte%62`); Rust is uniform.\n  - Rust has no zod `schema()`.\n- **permission.**\n  - Ported faithfully: modePolicy, readonlyBash (identical list), parseOverride, policy, wildcard, allStructured, evaluateBash.\n  - Differences: Rust `parse_action_value` rejects non-strings with different text, and Rust has no ask/respond/RejectedError/checkBashTokens.\n  - **Latent panic:** Rust `split_segments` slices `&command[i..i+2]` on byte indices (`permission.rs` L514), which panics on non-ASCII input such as `echo é && ls`.\n  - **Not wired:** no Rust tool consults the policy (X5).\n\n## 5. JS subsystems with no Rust counterpart\n- **agent**: agent definitions and system prompts.\n- **auth**: provider credentials and OAuth.\n- **bus**: event bus for session, part and permission events.\n- **command**: slash or user commands.\n- **file/time**: FileTime read stamps, read-before-edit assert and the per-file lock.\n- **file/ripgrep**: rg discovery, download and files/search wrapper.\n- **format**: post-edit formatters.\n- **mcp**: MCP client and tool timeouts.\n- **patch**: patch application.\n- **project/instance**: worktree and directory context.\n- **provider**: model providers, message sanitising and transforms.\n- **server**: HTTP server and API.\n- **session**: prompt loop, compaction, retry, summary, todo storage and processors.\n- **snapshot**: git snapshots and revert.\n- **storage**: persistent JSON storage.\n- **task tool**: sub-agent tool, absent from the Rust registry.\n- **json-standard claude output**: the Claude-compatible stream format.\n- **cli/cmd subcommands**: mcp, auth, models, agent, export, stats.\n- **continuous-mode / input queue**: stdin streaming and session resume/fork.\n- **verbose-fetch**: HTTP logging.\n- **config via lino-arguments / .lenv**: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env handling.\n- **util/bom**: BOM split/join.\n- **util/read-bounded**: bounded body reading (Rust uses inline equivalents).\n- **util/wildcard**: Rust has it only inside `permission.rs`.\n- **Binary.search/insert**: sorted-array helpers.\n- **Read-only / disable-tools tool filtering**: removes denied tools before a run.\n\n## 6. The worst gaps make the same tool call give a different result (grep, glob, todo, batch). The Rust CLI never runs tools or calls a model; it prints a ready message and stops. \"Br\" below says whether this branch caused the gap or it was already there before (pre-existing).\n\n**Prioritised divergences worth fixing (JS ↔ Rust)**\n\n1. **grep** (pre-existing; only the hidden-file change is from this branch). The two take different parameters, and Rust uses its own walker instead of rg.\n   - `grep.ts` L17-35 takes `{pattern, path, include}`; `grep.rs` L33-63 takes `{glob, output_mode=\"files_with_matches\", -i/-n/-A/-B/-C, head_limit}`.\n   - Rust silently ignores `include`, and by default it lists only file names.\n   - Rust output is `rel:N: line` with no header, sorting or 100 limit. Its metadata is `{count}` instead of `{matches, truncated}`.\n   - Rust follows symlinks (`grep.rs` L211), ignores .gitignore, and returns empty output instead of an error for a missing path.\n   - Its glob filter (L244-253) only understands `*.ext`.\n   - Fix: accept `include`, default to the JS output format, use the `ignore` crate or rg, and match the JS errors.\n2. **glob** (pre-existing; this branch added the Rust 100-result limit). `glob.rs` L69-120 differs from `glob.ts` L35-62 / `ripgrep.ts` L220-240.\n   - In Rust, `*.ts` matches the top level only (rg matches any depth), and `{a,b}` braces don't work.\n   - Rust follows symlinks, ignores .gitignore, and lists files inside `.git`.\n   - Rust prints relative paths and `\"\"` where JS prints absolute paths and \"No files found\".\n   - Rust sorts all results before cutting to 100; JS cuts first, then sorts.\n   - Fix: use `globset`/`ignore` with rg semantics.\n3. **todo** (pre-existing). A call shaped for JS fails in Rust.\n   - Rust `todo.rs` L19-39 requires `activeForm` and rejects `cancelled`.\n   - Rust drops the `id` and `priority` fields that JS has (`session/todo.ts` L6-19).\n   - Fix: align the Rust schema to JS.\n4. **batch bug** (pre-existing). `batch.rs` L118-128 uses `.take(MAX+1)`, so calls 12 and later disappear silently and the totals are wrong (`batch.ts` L39-40, L145-166).\n   - Fix: collect every call, then `split_off(MAX)`.\n   - Also: Rust runs calls one after another (JS in parallel) and has no disabled-tools check.\n5. **Rust tools have no permission or FileTime checks** (FileTime is JS's read-before-edit record). `permission.rs` is a faithful port, but only `cli.rs` L243-250 uses it.\n   - Missing in Rust edit and write: permission check, read-before-edit check, per-file lock.\n   - JS refs: `edit.ts` L69, L83, L106 and `write.ts` L30-53.\n   - Fix: call the policy from the tools and add a FileTime equivalent, or document the gap.\n6. **bash** (this branch). `bash.rs` L18, L98-175, L253-268 differs from `bash.ts` L21, L47-63, L236-301, L370-390.\n   - Default timeout is 120 s in Rust, 60 s in JS.\n   - Rust always uses `bash -c`; JS uses `$SHELL`.\n   - Rust passes stdin through, so a command that reads stdin can hang.\n   - Rust prints stdout, then a `--- stderr ---` block; JS interleaves them.\n   - Metadata keys differ: `{exitCode, command}` in Rust vs `{aborted, description}` in JS. [2026-11-02T23:31:25.835Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Memory and resource leak audit (issue #335)\n\nScope: `js/src` (primary, long-running CLI / continuous / server modes) and\n`rust/src` (tools + CLI). Read-only audit; no source file was edited.\nBun 1.4.4. Every finding below was checked against the surrounding code.\n\nSeverity: high = grows per tool call / LLM step in normal use; medium = per\nsession or per turn; low = bounded or one-off.\n\nExperiments (all in this directory; run from `js/` with\n`timeout 90 bun ../experiments/issue-335/audit/<file>.ts`):\n\n| Script | Result |\n| --- | --- |\n| `sse-usage-growth.ts` | 1000 simulated steps -> 1000 retained entries; one `consumeLatestUsage()` removes 1 (999 left). CONFIRMED |\n| `tee-no-cancel.ts` | 25 MB streamed response: peak extra RSS 25 MB when the usage branch only `break`s, 7 MB when it also cancels. CONFIRMED |\n| `abort-any-retention.ts` | `AbortSignal.any([longLived, ...])` + abort listener: 0/200 listener closures collected while the parent lives (200/200 without a listener, 200/200 once the timeout source fires). CONFIRMED |\n\n---\n\n## Confirmed\n\n### 1. `SSEUsageExtractor.pendingUsage` grows by one entry per LLM request (high)\n\n- Where: `js/src/util/sse-usage-extractor.ts:15` (`const pendingUsage = new Map()`).\n  Entries are added in `processStreamForUsage` (`:86`). The callers are\n  `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1212` (non-verbose path) and `:1385` (verbose path).\n- Resource: one `SSEUsageData` per streamed response that carries a usage\n  chunk. Small entries, but a module-level map that is never pruned.\n- Growth trigger: every LLM step whose SSE body carries usage. The only consumer\n  is `js/src/session/processor.ts:483` (`consumeLatestUsage()`). It runs only\n  when the AI SDK reported zero tokens, so with a normal provider nothing is\n  ever removed. Even when it does run, it removes only the newest entry.\n- Side effect (correctness): when the SDK does report 0 tokens,\n  `consumeLatestUsage` picks the newest entry across all sessions and requests.\n  With concurrent sessions in server mode, it can pick up another request's\n  usage.\n- Fix: return the request id with the response (or keep a per-request\n  callback) and `consumeUsage(id)` at finish-step. Minimal option: keep only\n  the latest entry (`pendingUsage.clear()` before `set`), or cap the map to the\n  last ~16 entries.\n\n### 2. Usage tee branch is abandoned without `cancel()` (medium: per-response duplication, released at stream end)\n\n- Where: `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1199-1216` (non-verbose path, the default).\n  ```ts\n  const [sdkStream, usageStream] = response.body.tee();\n  ... if (body.length > 50000) break;   // reader never cancelled\n  ```\n- Resource: the tee keeps queueing every later chunk into the unread\n  `usageStream` branch until the response ends. Peak memory for every LLM\n  response over 50 KB is therefore 2x the response size; the experiment\n  measured 25 MB extra for a 25 MB stream versus 7 MB with cancel.\n- Second effect: a tee source is cancelled only when *both* branches cancel.\n  If the SDK cancels its branch without aborting the fetch (for example it\n  stops consuming early), the HTTP body keeps downloading into the orphaned\n  branch.\n- Functional bug in the same spot: usage is normally in the last SSE chunk.\n  Cutting at the first 50 KB means long responses never yield usage, so the\n  #249 fallback silently fails for them.\n- Fix: after the loop, call `reader.cancel().catch(() => {})`. Do not\n  `await` it inline: by the Streams spec a tee branch's cancel promise settles\n  only when the other branch also cancels or the source closes. The first\n  version of the experiment deadlocked on exactly this. Better still, keep\n  reading to the end but retain only a rolling tail (for example the last 8 KB)\n  and parse usage from that.\n\n### 3. bash tool: command-stream keeps the whole output in memory, and the runner is pinned by an abort listener (high for large outputs)\n\n- Where: `js/src/tool/bash.ts:231-232` and `:296-300`.\n  ```ts\n  const timeoutSignal = [REDACTED];           // 60 s default, 10 min max\n  const cancel = AbortSignal.any([ctx.abort, timeoutSignal]);\n  new ProcessRunner(..., { signal: [REDACTED]\n  ```\n- Resource, part (a): unbounded buffering. `capture: true` makes\n  command-stream push every stdout and stderr chunk into\n  `runner.outChunks/errChunks`. See command-stream 2.6.0\n  `src/$.process-runner-execution.mjs:291,331`. At exit it also builds\n  `Buffer.concat(...).toString()` (`:461-468`).\n\n  bash.ts carefully keeps only `2 * MAX_BYTES` of output (`:234-249`), but the\n  runner holds the full output twice. A command that prints 500 MB costs about\n  1 GB. bash.ts only reads `command.result.child.signalCode` from the result.\n- Resource, part (b): retention. `setupExternalAbortSignal` (`:545`) adds\n  `signal.addEventListener('abort', () => stopForAbort(runner))` and never\n  removes it. Bun keeps an `AbortSignal.any` dependent that has a listener\n  alive while a source is alive; the `abort-any-retention.ts` experiment showed\n  0/200 closures collected.\n\n  So the runner and its captured buffers outlive the tool call until the\n  timeout fires (60 s to 10 min) or the turn ends. `prompt.ts` aborts the\n  per-loop controller in `cancel()` via `defer`. In a busy turn, every bash call\n  of the last 60 s or more stays resident at once.\n- Growth trigger: every bash tool call (default timeout 60 s).\n- Fix: pass `capture: false`. The tool consumes `command.stream()` chunks\n  itself. Confirm that the `stream()` and `result.child` paths still work with\n  capture off in the pinned version. Also give the runner its own\n  `AbortController`, link it with a listener that bash.ts removes in a\n  `finally`, and abort the private controller in the `finally` so command-stream's\n  listener is released immediately.\n- Version note: `bun.lock` pins command-stream 2.4.0. Only 2.6.0 is in the\n  local Bun cache, so the line numbers above are from 2.6.0. Re-check 2.4.0\n  when node_modules is installed.\n\n---\n\n## Verified by reading (not reproduced)\n\n### 4. grep tool reads all of rg's output, parses and stats every match, then keeps 100 (medium)\n\n- `js/src/tool/grep.ts:81-83`: `new Response(proc.stdout).text()` buffers the\n  complete `rg --json` output. A broad pattern in a large repo can produce\n  hundreds of MB.\n- `:119-153`: every match is JSON-parsed and `stat`ed one at a time, but only\n  100 are returned (`:157`). The match lines themselves are not truncated\n  until formatting.\n- `:69-77`: the same `AbortSignal.timeout(30 s)` + `any([ctx.abort, ...])`\n  pattern, passed to `Bun.spawn({ signal })`. This may pin the subprocess\n  object for up to 30 s; low.\n- Fix: stream stdout line by line and stop (kill rg) after N matches. Or pass\n  `--max-count`/`--max-columns 2000 --max-columns-preview` and cap the bytes\n  read, as `Ripgrep.files()` already does in `js/src/file/ripgrep.ts`.\n\n### 5. `FileTime.state().read` is never pruned per session (medium)\n\n- `js/src/file/time.ts:21-31,66-67`: `read[sessionID][path] = stamp`.\n- Trigger: every distinct file read or written in every session, including\n  subagent (task) sessions. It is freed only on `Instance.dispose`. In server\n  mode or a long continuous run with many sessions this grows without bound.\n  The per-entry size is small.\n- Fix: delete `read[sessionID]` when a session is deleted or archived, and for\n  subagent sessions when the task tool finishes. Alternatively, cap the number\n  of sessions kept (LRU).\n\n### 6. Continuous mode: per-message idle subscription leaks if `session.idle` never fires (low)\n\n- `js/src/cli/continuous-mode.js:360-369` and `:586-595`: `checkIdle =\n  Bus.subscribeAll(...)`, removed only inside the idle handler.\n- `SessionPrompt.prompt` (`js/src/session/prompt.ts:252-263`) can throw before\n  `loop()` runs: `Session.get`, `SessionRevert.cleanup` or `createUserMessage`.\n  No idle event is published on that path. The subscription then stays forever,\n  and `await messagePromise` hangs the input queue, because `isProcessing` is\n  never reset.\n- Fix: unsubscribe and resolve in the `.catch` of the prompt promise as well,\n  for example with `Promise.race([messagePromise, promptPromise])` plus a\n  `finally(checkIdle)`.\n\n### 7. Upstream retry paths drop error responses without cancelling the body (low)\n\n- `js/src/provider/retry-fetch.ts:463` (5xx retry) and `:556` (429 retry). The\n  `Response` from the failed attempt is discarded and its body is neither read\n  nor cancelled. The connection and buffer are released only by GC. Bodies\n  are usually small.\n- Fix: `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => {})` before\n  `sleep(...)`/`continue`.\n\n### 8. `SessionRetry.sleep` leaves its abort listener attached after the delay elapses (low)\n\n- `js/src/session/retry.ts:130-143`. Called from\n  `js/src/session/processor.ts:805` with the turn's abort signal. Each retry\n  adds a listener (`{ once: true }` only removes it after abort). The listeners\n  are bounded by the retry count and released when the turn ends.\n- Fix: `setTimeout(() => { signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort); resolve(); }, ...)`.\n  `retry-fetch.ts:179-216` already does this correctly.\n\n### 9. `withTimeout` keeps the timer when the wrapped promise rejects (low)\n\n- `js/src/util/timeout.ts:4-7`. `clearTimeout` runs only on fulfilment, so a\n  rejected MCP call (`js/src/mcp/index.ts:610-620`) leaves an unref'd timer\n  and its closure alive until the timeout.\n- Fix: use `promise.finally(() => clearTimeout(timeout))`.\n\n### 10. `Instance.dispose()` leaves the directory in `cache` (low)\n\n- `js/src/project/instance.ts:13,58-62`. `dispose()` disposes the state but does\n  not `cache.delete(directory)`, so the resolved `Context` stays. Only\n  `disposeAll()` clears it (`:73`). One entry per directory ever served\n  (server mode with per-request `directory`).\n- Fix: `cache.delete(Instance.directory)` in `dispose()`.\n\n### 11. Pending permission asks are not dropped on session abort (low)\n\n- `js/src/permission/index.ts:383-390`. `pending[sessionID][id]` holds a\n  promise and its resolve and reject functions until answered or until\n  `Instance` is disposed (`:320-330`). An aborted turn that was waiting on\n  `ask` leaves its entry behind.\n- Fix: reject and delete the entries for a session when its abort signal fires\n  (`SessionPrompt.cancel`).\n\n### 12. Server: client disconnect does not cancel the turn (low to medium)\n\n- `js/src/server/server.ts:195-201`. `POST /session/:id/message` awaits\n  `SessionPrompt.prompt` inside `stream()`. When the HTTP client disconnects,\n  the turn, with its LLM stream and tools, keeps running to completion.\n- Fix: `stream.onAbort(() => SessionPrompt.cancel(sessionID))`.\n\n### 13. Optional per-request provider timeout signal (low)\n\n- `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1131-1137`. This is `AbortSignal.any([init.signal,\n  AbortSignal.timeout(t)])` per request, only when a provider `timeout` is\n  configured. The SDK's listeners on it are pinned until the timeout fires.\n  This is the same mechanism as item 3, but no large buffers are attached.\n\n### Rust (`rust/src`)\n\n### R1. bash timeout kills only the shell, not its process tree (medium)\n\n- `rust/src/tool/bash.rs:111-139`. The child is spawned without\n  `process_group(0)`/`setsid`, and `child.kill()` sends SIGKILL to `bash` only.\n  Background or pipeline grandchildren (`cmd &`, `a | b`, servers) survive as\n  orphans after every timed-out call.\n- Second effect: if a grandchild inherits stdout, `pump` never sees EOF after\n  `bash` exits. The call then always waits for the full timeout.\n- Fix: `cmd.process_group(0)` (tokio `Command::process_group`, Unix). On\n  timeout, `libc::killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)`. On Windows, use a job object or\n  `taskkill /T`.\n- Output buffering is fine. `Capture` keeps at most `4 * MAX_BYTES` per stream\n  (`:209-222`).\n\n### R2. Rust grep loads whole files and collects unlimited results (low to medium)\n\n- `rust/src/tool/grep.rs:158-197,204-240`. `collect_files` walks everything\n  except `.git`, with `follow_links(true)` and no `.gitignore` handling. It\n  then runs `fs::read_to_string` on every file, a blocking call on the async\n  runtime. `results` is unbounded unless the caller passes `head_limit`.\n- Fix: default the limit (for example 100 entries, as in JS), skip files over a\n  size cap, honour ignore files (the `ignore` crate), and use\n  `spawn_blocking`.\n\n### R3. Rust read loads the whole file before slicing (low)\n\n- `rust/src/tool/read.rs` (`async_fs::read(&filepath)` after the binary\n  sample). This is a one-off per call, but a multi-GB file is fully\n  materialized.\n- Fix: read with a `BufReader` line by line up to `offset + limit`.\n\n---\n\n## Checked and found OK (not leaks)\n\n- `session/prompt.ts` `state` per session: removed via\n  `using _ = defer(() => cancel(sessionID))`.\n- `session/status.ts`: the entry is deleted on idle.\n- `session/retry.ts` `retryStates`: cleared on finish, on non-retryable errors\n  and on overflow.\n- `tool/task.ts`: the abort listener is removed via `defer`, and Bus `unsub`\n  runs in a `finally`.\n- `tool/webfetch.ts`: bodies are cancelled and `readBounded` caps the read;\n  the timeout signal is [REDACTED]\n- `file/ripgrep.ts` `files()`: the `finally` cancels the reader, kills rg and\n  awaits exit.\n- `mcp/index.ts`: state dispose closes clients and kills descendants; failed\n  clients are closed in `tools()`.\n- `bus/index.ts` unsubscribe, `util/lock.ts` (empty locks removed),\n  `util/log.ts` (one logger per service), `util/verbose-fetch.ts` (log tee\n  read to the end).\n- `provider/model-discovery.ts` caches: bounded.\n- `provider/retry-fetch.ts` own `sleep` and `createIsolatedRateLimitSignal`:\n  cleaned up in `finally`.\n- `tool/tool.ts` `define`: wrapper accumulation already fixed (see\n  `../bash-web/define-accumulation.ts`).\n- `session/processor.ts:258` calls `MessageV2.parts()` per tool-call event for\n  doom-loop detection. Re-check of the README §4–§5 \"n/a\" Rust entries\n- **grep.** Rust uses its own WalkDir + regex walker, not rg. The rg-specific fixes (exit 2, pipe, timeout, `--no-config`) genuinely are n/a. However, the walker **follows symlinks** (`grep.rs` L211) and **ignores .gitignore**; record these as divergences, not n/a.\n- **read relative paths.** **Not n/a.** Rust resolves them via `ctx.resolve_path` (`read.rs` L115). Rust's lack of `..` normalisation differs from `path.resolve`.\n- **glob symlinks.** Rust (`glob` crate) **follows** symlinks; JS rg does not. Not n/a. Rust list uses `follow_links(false)`, which matches JS.\n- **FileTime read-before-edit.** Rust has **no** FileTime, so it has no read-before-edit check, no lock and no read stamps. This is a real behavioural divergence, not n/a.\n- **\"bash already bash\".** Outdated: JS now picks `$SHELL`.\n- **HTML script/style skipping.** Rust only handles bare tags; tags with attributes leak their content.\n- **\"replaceAll literal\".** Correct.\n\n## 3. CLI and JSON I/O (`js/src/index.js`, `js/src/cli/**`, `js/src/config/config.ts` ↔ `rust/src/cli.rs`)\n- **Options only in JS.**\n  - `--read-only` and `--disable-tools` (`cli/run-options.js` L216-226).\n  - Subcommands `mcp`, `auth`, `models`, `agent`, `export`, `stats` (index.js L655-661, `cli/cmd/*`).\n  - The middleware mapping `--output-format` to `json-standard` (run-options.js L144-159).\n- **Options only in Rust.** `--working-directory`.\n- **Accepted but no-op in Rust.** `--json-standard claude`, `--input-format`, and `InputMessage.tools`.\n- **Execution.** The Rust CLI **never executes tools or calls a model**. `run_with_input` prints \"Agent (Rust) ready…\" text and finishes with `step_finish{reason:\"stop\"}`.\n- **Env vars read by JS only** (`config/config.ts`, plus `.lenv` via lino-arguments): every `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` variable for\n  - VERBOSE, DRY_RUN, GENERATE_TITLE, OUTPUT_RESPONSE_MODEL, SUMMARIZE_SESSION, COMPACT_JSON\n  - CONFIG, CONFIG_DIR, CONFIG_CONTENT\n  - DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, DISABLE_PRUNE, ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_MODELS, DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT, EXPERIMENTAL, EXPERIMENTAL_WATCHER\n  - RETRY_TIMEOUT, MAX_RETRY_DELAY, MIN_RETRY_INTERVAL, STREAM_CHUNK/STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, MCP_DEFAULT/MAX_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT\n  - VERIFY_IMAGES_AT_READ_TOOL, **READ_ONLY**, **DISABLE_TOOLS**\n- **Env vars read by Rust.** Only DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_COMPACTION_MODEL(S), DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SAFETY_MARGIN_PERCENT (`defaults.rs`), and PERMISSION_MODE / PERMISSION (`permission.rs` L35-65).\n- **Events emitted by JS.** status, step_start, text, tool_use, tool_result, step_finish, error, input, init, config, idle, session_idle, log, message, permission_request, result, warning.\n  - Envelopes carry `{type, timestamp, sessionID, part}` (`cli/event-handler.js` L57-145). Resume `status` events add mode, sessionID, title and forked (`continuous-mode.js` L200-230).\n- **Events emitted by Rust** (`OutputEvent`, cli.rs L271-315):\n  - status, step_start, text, step_finish, error, plus tool_use, which is defined but never emitted.\n  - `error` is `{timestamp, sessionID:null, error{name,data}}`, and step parts are synthetic.\n\n## 4. Utilities\n- **binary.** These are unrelated modules that share a name.\n  - JS `util/binary.ts` provides `Binary.search/insert` over sorted arrays, which has no Rust counterpart.\n  - Rust `util/binary.rs` holds binary/image detection, ported from read.ts `isBinaryFile` (L481-542), `isImageFile` (L365-390) and `validateImageFormat` (L401-452). The port is equivalent.\n- **filesystem.**\n  - **BUG:** Rust `contains` (`util/filesystem.rs` L52-65) canonicalises, which follows symlinks. When a path does not exist it falls back to a **string prefix**, so `contains(\"/a/b\",\"/a/bc\")` returns true. JS `util/filesystem.ts` uses a lexical `relative()`, which returns false.\n  - Rust `overlaps` is component-based; JS uses string `startsWith('..')`.\n  - Rust lacks `up`/`globUp` (JS L29-72).\n  - The Rust `Filesystem` module is unused.\n- **id.**\n  - Same format and algorithm, and Rust adds `Prefix::Call`.\n  - Rust panics where JS throws; for example, given `\"\"` JS generates a new id while Rust panics.\n  - Rust's counter does a non-atomic load-then-store.\n  - JS `randomBase62` is modulo-biased (`byte%62`); Rust is uniform.\n  - Rust has no zod `schema()`.\n- **permission.**\n  - Ported faithfully: modePolicy, readonlyBash (identical list), parseOverride, policy, wildcard, allStructured, evaluateBash.\n  - Differences: Rust `parse_action_value` rejects non-strings with different text, and Rust has no ask/respond/RejectedError/checkBashTokens.\n  - **Latent panic:** Rust `split_segments` slices `&command[i..i+2]` on byte indices (`permission.rs` L514), which panics on non-ASCII input such as `echo é && ls`.\n  - **Not wired:** no Rust tool consults the policy (X5).\n\n## 5. JS subsystems with no Rust counterpart\n- **agent**: agent definitions and system prompts.\n- **auth**: provider credentials and OAuth.\n- **bus**: event bus for session, part and permission events.\n- **command**: slash or user commands.\n- **file/time**: FileTime read stamps, read-before-edit assert and the per-file lock.\n- **file/ripgrep**: rg discovery, download and files/search wrapper.\n- **format**: post-edit formatters.\n- **mcp**: MCP client and tool timeouts.\n- **patch**: patch application.\n- **project/instance**: worktree and directory context.\n- **provider**: model providers, message sanitising and transforms.\n- **server**: HTTP server and API.\n- **session**: prompt loop, compaction, retry, summary, todo storage and processors.\n- **snapshot**: git snapshots and revert.\n- **storage**: persistent JSON storage.\n- **task tool**: sub-agent tool, absent from the Rust registry.\n- **json-standard claude output**: the Claude-compatible stream format.\n- **cli/cmd subcommands**: mcp, auth, models, agent, export, stats.\n- **continuous-mode / input queue**: stdin streaming and session resume/fork.\n- **verbose-fetch**: HTTP logging.\n- **config via lino-arguments / .lenv**: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env handling.\n- **util/bom**: BOM split/join.\n- **util/read-bounded**: bounded body reading (Rust uses inline equivalents).\n- **util/wildcard**: Rust has it only inside `permission.rs`.\n- **Binary.search/insert**: sorted-array helpers.\n- **Read-only / disable-tools tool filtering**: removes denied tools before a run.\n\n## 6. Prioritised fix list\n1. **grep.** Accept JS `include` (alias to `glob`), default to content output in the JS format (\"Found N matches\", grouped by file, mtime sort, 100 limit, \"No files found\"), and set metadata `{matches,truncated}`. Either use rg or the `ignore` crate (.gitignore, no symlink following), and error on a missing path. `grep.rs` L33-63, L200-330 ↔ `grep.ts` L17-140.\n2. **glob.** Use the `ignore`/`globset` crates with rg semantics (a slash-less pattern matches at any depth, braces, .gitignore, exclude `.git`, no follow). Print absolute paths and \"No files found\", and take the first 100 before sorting. `glob.rs` L69-120 ↔ `glob.ts` L35-62, `ripgrep.ts` L220-240.\n3. **todo.** Align the schema: add `cancelled`, `priority` and `id`; make `activeForm` optional or drop it; use the description from `todowrite.txt`. `todo.rs` L19-39 ↔ `session/todo.ts` L6-19.\n4. **batch.** Collect every call and then `split_off(MAX)`. `batch.rs` L118-128 ↔ `batch.ts` L39-40, L145-166. Consider parallel execution.\n5. **Permissions and FileTime in Rust tools.** Call `permission.rs` from edit, write, bash and webfetch, and add a FileTime equivalent (read stamp, assert before edit, lock), or document the gap. `edit.rs`, `write.rs` ↔ `edit.ts` L69-106, `write.ts` L30-53.\n6. **bash.**\n   - Set the default timeout to 60 000 ms.\n   - Set stdin to null.\n   - Use the `$SHELL` selection (excluding fish and nu).\n   - Interleave stdout and stderr.\n   - Use metadata keys `{output, exit, signal, timedOut, aborted, description}` and the JS timeout text.\n   - Kill the process tree.\n\n   `bash.rs` L18, L98-175, L253-268 ↔ `bash.ts` L21, L47-63, L236-301, L370-390.\n7. **read.** Make an empty file count as 1 line, use JS line splitting (`/\\r?\\n/`, pop the trailing empty line), strip the BOM, apply NFC in canonical_name, and accept numeric strings. `read.rs` L115-177, L346-354 ↔ `read.ts` L23-38, L261-276.\n8. **edit.**\n   - Use the \"File X not found\" and \"Path is a directory\" messages.\n   - Add BOM split/join.\n   - Keep the original endings in filediff.\n   - Produce a unified diff with `@@` headers.\n   - BlockAnchor should pick the best candidate.\n   - Apply the disproportionate-match check to all replacers and throw on it.\n   - Check uniqueness for fuzzy matches.\n\n   `edit.rs` L82-546 ↔ `edit.ts` L19-154, L250-713.\n9. **list.** Use glob-based prefix ignores, respect .gitignore, treat user ignore entries as globs, drop the extra truncation note, and use the JS error texts. `list.rs` L17-41, L111-123, L193-252 ↔ `ls.ts` L8-33, L119.\n10. **webfetch.** Fix script/style skipping when the tag has attributes. Port Turndown-like markdown or use `html2md`. Use the JS status text (\"404\") and timeout text, and add `text/markdown;q=0.7`. Make the tag removal safe for non-ASCII. `webfetch.rs` L157, L196-335 ↔ `webfetch.ts` L60-220.\n11. **CLI.** Add `--read-only`, `--disable-tools` and the `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_READ_ONLY/DISABLE_TOOLS` env vars (a registry filter); add the `timestamp/sessionID/part` envelope; or document that the Rust CLI is a non-executing stub. `cli.rs` L243-470 ↔ `run-options.js` L144-226, `event-handler.js` L57-145.\n12. **Latent panics and bugs.** Fix the `split_segments` byte-index slicing (`permission.rs` L514) and the `Filesystem::contains` string-prefix fallback (`util/filesystem.rs` L59-64) vs `filesystem.ts` `contains`. The id panic on `\"\"` should fall back to generating a new id.\n13. **Minor.**\n    - websearch: `numResults` 0 should become 8; validate the enums; use the JS status text; port the description.\n    - codesearch: validate `tokensNum` rather than clamping.\n    - multiedit: handle `edits: []` in JS.\n14. **Docs.** `rust/README.md` claims 7 tools, but all of them exist. Re-check of the README §4–§5 \"n/a\" Rust entries\n- **grep.** Rust uses its own WalkDir + regex walker, not rg. The rg-specific fixes (exit 2, pipe, timeout, `--no-config`) genuinely are n/a. However, the walker **follows symlinks** (`grep.rs` L211) and **ignores .gitignore**; record these as divergences, not n/a.\n- **read relative paths.** **Not n/a.** Rust resolves them via `ctx.resolve_path` (`read.rs` L115). Rust's lack of `..` normalisation differs from `path.resolve`.\n- **glob symlinks.** Rust (`glob` crate) **follows** symlinks; JS rg does not. Not n/a. Rust list uses `follow_links(false)`, which matches JS.\n- **FileTime read-before-edit.** Rust has **no** FileTime, so it has no read-before-edit check, no lock and no read stamps. This is a real behavioural divergence, not n/a.\n- **\"bash already bash\".** Outdated: JS now picks `$SHELL`.\n- **HTML script/style skipping.** Rust only handles bare tags; tags with attributes leak their content.\n- **\"replaceAll literal\".** Correct.\n\n## 3. CLI and JSON I/O (`js/src/index.js`, `js/src/cli/**`, `js/src/config/config.ts` ↔ `rust/src/cli.rs`)\n- **Options only in JS.**\n  - `--read-only` and `--disable-tools` (`cli/run-options.js` L216-226).\n  - Subcommands `mcp`, `auth`, `models`, `agent`, `export`, `stats` (index.js L655-661, `cli/cmd/*`).\n  - The middleware mapping `--output-format` to `json-standard` (run-options.js L144-159).\n- **Options only in Rust.** `--working-directory`.\n- **Accepted but no-op in Rust.** `--json-standard claude`, `--input-format`, and `InputMessage.tools`.\n- **Execution.** The Rust CLI **never executes tools or calls a model**. `run_with_input` prints \"Agent (Rust) ready…\" text and finishes with `step_finish{reason:\"stop\"}`.\n- **Env vars read by JS only** (`config/config.ts`, plus `.lenv` via lino-arguments): every `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` variable for\n  - VERBOSE, DRY_RUN, GENERATE_TITLE, OUTPUT_RESPONSE_MODEL, SUMMARIZE_SESSION, COMPACT_JSON\n  - CONFIG, CONFIG_DIR, CONFIG_CONTENT\n  - DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, DISABLE_PRUNE, ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_MODELS, DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT, EXPERIMENTAL, EXPERIMENTAL_WATCHER\n  - RETRY_TIMEOUT, MAX_RETRY_DELAY, MIN_RETRY_INTERVAL, STREAM_CHUNK/STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, MCP_DEFAULT/MAX_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT\n  - VERIFY_IMAGES_AT_READ_TOOL, **READ_ONLY**, **DISABLE_TOOLS**\n- **Env vars read by Rust.** Only DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_COMPACTION_MODEL(S), DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SAFETY_MARGIN_PERCENT (`defaults.rs`), and PERMISSION_MODE / PERMISSION (`permission.rs` L35-65).\n- **Events emitted by JS.** status, step_start, text, tool_use, tool_result, step_finish, error, input, init, config, idle, session_idle, log, message, permission_request, result, warning.\n  - Envelopes carry `{type, timestamp, sessionID, part}` (`cli/event-handler.js` L57-145). Resume `status` events add mode, sessionID, title and forked (`continuous-mode.js` L200-230).\n- **Events emitted by Rust** (`OutputEvent`, cli.rs L271-315):\n  - status, step_start, text, step_finish, error, plus tool_use, which is defined but never emitted.\n  - `error` is `{timestamp, sessionID:null, error{name,data}}`, and step parts are synthetic.\n\n## 4. Utilities\n- **binary.** These are unrelated modules that share a name.\n  - JS `util/binary.ts` provides `Binary.search/insert` over sorted arrays, which has no Rust counterpart.\n  - Rust `util/binary.rs` holds binary/image detection, ported from read.ts `isBinaryFile` (L481-542), `isImageFile` (L365-390) and `validateImageFormat` (L401-452). The port is equivalent.\n- **filesystem.**\n  - **BUG:** Rust `contains` (`util/filesystem.rs` L52-65) canonicalises, which follows symlinks. When a path does not exist it falls back to a **string prefix**, so `contains(\"/a/b\",\"/a/bc\")` returns true. JS `util/filesystem.ts` uses a lexical `relative()`, which returns false.\n  - Rust `overlaps` is component-based; JS uses string `startsWith('..')`.\n  - Rust lacks `up`/`globUp` (JS L29-72).\n  - The Rust `Filesystem` module is unused.\n- **id.**\n  - Same format and algorithm, and Rust adds `Prefix::Call`.\n  - Rust panics where JS throws; for example, given `\"\"` JS generates a new id while Rust panics.\n  - Rust's counter does a non-atomic load-then-store.\n  - JS `randomBase62` is modulo-biased (`byte%62`); Rust is uniform.\n  - Rust has no zod `schema()`.\n- **permission.**\n  - Ported faithfully: modePolicy, readonlyBash (identical list), parseOverride, policy, wildcard, allStructured, evaluateBash.\n  - Differences: Rust `parse_action_value` rejects non-strings with different text, and Rust has no ask/respond/RejectedError/checkBashTokens.\n  - **Latent panic:** Rust `split_segments` slices `&command[i..i+2]` on byte indices (`permission.rs` L514), which panics on non-ASCII input such as `echo é && ls`.\n  - **Not wired:** no Rust tool consults the policy (X5).\n\n## 5. JS subsystems with no Rust counterpart\n- **agent**: agent definitions and system prompts.\n- **auth**: provider credentials and OAuth.\n- **bus**: event bus for session, part and permission events.\n- **command**: slash or user commands.\n- **file/time**: FileTime read stamps, read-before-edit assert and the per-file lock.\n- **file/ripgrep**: rg discovery, download and files/search wrapper.\n- **format**: post-edit formatters.\n- **mcp**: MCP client and tool timeouts.\n- **patch**: patch application.\n- **project/instance**: worktree and directory context.\n- **provider**: model providers, message sanitising and transforms.\n- **server**: HTTP server and API.\n- **session**: prompt loop, compaction, retry, summary, todo storage and processors.\n- **snapshot**: git snapshots and revert.\n- **storage**: persistent JSON storage.\n- **task tool**: sub-agent tool, absent from the Rust registry.\n- **json-standard claude output**: the Claude-compatible stream format.\n- **cli/cmd subcommands**: mcp, auth, models, agent, export, stats.\n- **continuous-mode / input queue**: stdin streaming and session resume/fork.\n- **verbose-fetch**: HTTP logging.\n- **config via lino-arguments / .lenv**: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env handling.\n- **util/bom**: BOM split/join.\n- **util/read-bounded**: bounded body reading (Rust uses inline equivalents).\n- **util/wildcard**: Rust has it only inside `permission.rs`.\n- **Binary.search/insert**: sorted-array helpers.\n- **Read-only / disable-tools tool filtering**: removes denied tools before a run.\n\n## 6. Prioritised fix list\n1. **grep.** Accept JS `include` (alias to `glob`), default to content output in the JS format (\"Found N matches\", grouped by file, mtime sort, 100 limit, \"No files found\"), and set metadata `{matches,truncated}`. Either use rg or the `ignore` crate (.gitignore, no symlink following), and error on a missing path. `grep.rs` L33-63, L200-330 ↔ `grep.ts` L17-140.\n2. **glob.** Use the `ignore`/`globset` crates with rg semantics (a slash-less pattern matches at any depth, braces, .gitignore, exclude `.git`, no follow). Print absolute paths and \"No files found\", and take the first 100 before sorting. `glob.rs` L69-120 ↔ `glob.ts` L35-62, `ripgrep.ts` L220-240.\n3. **todo.** Align the schema: add `cancelled`, `priority` and `id`; make `activeForm` optional or drop it; use the description from `todowrite.txt`. `todo.rs` L19-39 ↔ `session/todo.ts` L6-19.\n4. **batch.** Collect every call and then `split_off(MAX)`. `batch.rs` L118-128 ↔ `batch.ts` L39-40, L145-166. Consider parallel execution.\n5. **Permissions and FileTime in Rust tools.** Call `permission.rs` from edit, write, bash and webfetch, and add a FileTime equivalent (read stamp, assert before edit, lock), or document the gap. `edit.rs`, `write.rs` ↔ `edit.ts` L69-106, `write.ts` L30-53.\n6. **bash.**\n   - Set the default timeout to 60 000 ms.\n   - Set stdin to null.\n   - Use the `$SHELL` selection (excluding fish and nu).\n   - Interleave stdout and stderr.\n   - Use metadata keys `{output, exit, signal, timedOut, aborted, description}` and the JS timeout text.\n   - Kill the process tree.\n\n   `bash.rs` L18, L98-175, L253-268 ↔ `bash.ts` L21, L47-63, L236-301, L370-390.\n7. **read.** Make an empty file count as 1 line, use JS line splitting (`/\\r?\\n/`, pop the trailing empty line), strip the BOM, apply NFC in canonical_name, and accept numeric strings. `read.rs` L115-177, L346-354 ↔ `read.ts` L23-38, L261-276.\n8. **edit.**\n   - Use the \"File X not found\" and \"Path is a directory\" messages.\n   - Add BOM split/join.\n   - Keep the original endings in filediff.\n   - Produce a unified diff with `@@` headers.\n   - BlockAnchor should pick the best candidate.\n   - Apply the disproportionate-match check to all replacers and throw on it.\n   - Check uniqueness for fuzzy matches.\n\n   `edit.rs` L82-546 ↔ `edit.ts` L19-154, L250-713.\n9. **list.** Use glob-based prefix ignores, respect .gitignore, treat user ignore entries as globs, drop the extra truncation note, and use the JS error texts. `list.rs` L17-41, L111-123, L193-252 ↔ `ls.ts` L8-33, L119.\n10. **webfetch.** Fix script/style skipping when the tag has attributes. Port Turndown-like markdown or use `html2md`. Use the JS status text (\"404\") and timeout text, and add `text/markdown;q=0.7`. Make the tag removal safe for non-ASCII. `webfetch.rs` L157, L196-335 ↔ `webfetch.ts` L60-220.\n11. **CLI.** Add `--read-only`, `--disable-tools` and the `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_READ_ONLY/DISABLE_TOOLS` env vars (a registry filter); add the `timestamp/sessionID/part` envelope; or document that the Rust CLI is a non-executing stub. `cli.rs` L243-470 ↔ `run-options.js` L144-226, `event-handler.js` L57-145.\n12. **Latent panics and bugs.** Fix the `split_segments` byte-index slicing (`permission.rs` L514) and the `Filesystem::contains` string-prefix fallback (`util/filesystem.rs` L59-64) vs `filesystem.ts` `contains`. The id panic on `\"\"` should fall back to generating a new id.\n13. **Minor.**\n    - websearch: `numResults` 0 should become 8; validate the enums; use the JS status text; port the description.\n    - codesearch: validate `tokensNum` rather than clamping.\n    - multiedit: handle `edits: []` in JS.\n14. **Docs.** `rust/README.md` claims 7 tools, but all of them exist. No source files were edited. The full report is at `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-1793661506571/experiments/issue-335/audit/memory-leak-audit.md`.\n\n**Confirmed by experiment** (scripts are in the same `audit/` folder; run from `js/` with `timeout 90 bun ../experiments/issue-335/audit/<file>.ts`):\n\n1. **Usage map grows on every LLM request (high).**\n   - Where: `js/src/util/sse-usage-extractor.ts:15` (`pendingUsage`), filled from `provider/provider.ts:1212` and `:1390`.\n   - Cause: the only thing that removes entries is `session/processor.ts:483`. It runs only when the SDK reports zero tokens, and then removes just one entry. With concurrent sessions it can also pick up another request's usage.\n   - Evidence: `sse-usage-growth.ts` kept 1000 entries after 1000 steps, and one consume left 999.\n   - Fix: consume by request id, or keep only the latest entry, or cap the map.\n2. **Usage stream copy is dropped without being cancelled (medium).**\n   - Where: `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1199-1216`. After 50 KB the loop just stops reading.\n   - Effect: that copy keeps buffering the rest of the response, so every LLM response over 50 KB takes twice its size in memory until it ends.\n   - Evidence: `tee-no-cancel.ts` showed 25 MB extra memory for a 25 MB stream, against 7 MB when the copy is cancelled.\n   - Side bug: usage normally arrives at the end of the stream, so long responses never yield it.\n   - Fix: call `reader.cancel().catch(()=>{})` without `await`. An awaited cancel here waits for the other copy too, and my first version of the experiment deadlocked on it. Better still, read to the end and keep only the last part.\n3. **The bash tool holds the full command output, and keeps it after the call (high for large outputs).**\n   - Where: `js/src/tool/bash.ts:231-232` and `:296-300`.\n   - Cause: `capture: true` makes command-stream store all stdout and stderr, plus a second full copy at exit. `bash.ts` itself keeps only `2*MAX_BYTES`. command-stream also adds an abort listener it never removes.\n   - Evidence: `abort-any-retention.ts` showed 0 of 200 listener closures freed while the session signal was [REDACTED]\n   - Effect: each runner and its buffers stay in memory until the 60 s to 10 min timeout fires or the turn ends.\n   - Fix: pass `capture: false`, and give the runner its own controller that is aborted and unlinked in a `finally`.\n   - Caveat: I checked command-stream 2.6.0, the only version in the local Bun cache. `bun.lock` pins 2.4.0, so this needs re-checking once dependencies are installed.\n\n**Confirmed by reading only:**\n\n4. **grep tool output is unbounded (medium).** `js/src/tool/grep.ts:81-83` reads all of ripgrep's output into memory. Lines 119-153 then parse and stat every match before keeping 100. Fix: stream and stop at N matches, or pass ripgrep's per-file match and line-length limits.\n5. **File read times never pruned (medium).** `js/src/file/time.ts:21-31,66-67` grows per file per session, including subagent sessions, until the instance is disposed. Fix: drop a session's entries when it ends.\n6. **Continuous mode can hang (low).** In `js/src/cli/continuous-mode.js:360-369` and `:586-595`, if `SessionPrompt.prompt` throws before its loop starts, `session.idle` never fires. The subscription then leaks and the input queue stops.\n7. **Retried error responses not cancelled (low).** `js/src/provider/retry-fetch.ts:463` (5xx) and `:556` (429) drop the response body without cancelling it.\n8. **Retry sleep leaves its abort listener attached (low).** `js/src/session/retry.ts:130-143`. `retry-fetch.ts` already does this correctly.\n9. **`withTimeout` keeps its timer on rejection (low).** `js/src/util/timeout.ts:4-7`; this affects MCP calls. Fix: clear it in `.finally`.\n10. **`Instance.dispose()` leaves its cache entry (low).** `js/src/project/instance.ts:58-62` never deletes the directory from the cache.\n11. **Pending permission asks survive an abort (low).** `js/src/permission/index.ts:383-390`.\n12. **Server doesn't cancel on disconnect (low to medium).** In `js/src/server/server.ts:195-201`, a client disconnect does not cancel the running turn. Re-check of the README §4–§5 \"n/a\" Rust entries\n- **grep.** Rust uses its own WalkDir + regex walker, not rg. The rg-specific fixes (exit 2, pipe, timeout, `--no-config`) genuinely are n/a. However, the walker **follows symlinks** (`grep.rs` L211) and **ignores .gitignore**; record these as divergences, not n/a.\n- **read relative paths.** **Not n/a.** Rust resolves them via `ctx.resolve_path` (`read.rs` L115). Rust's lack of `..` normalisation differs from `path.resolve`.\n- **glob symlinks.** Rust (`glob` crate) **follows** symlinks; JS rg does not. Not n/a. Rust list uses `follow_links(false)`, which matches JS.\n- **FileTime read-before-edit.** Rust has **no** FileTime, so it has no read-before-edit check, no lock and no read stamps. This is a real behavioural divergence, not n/a.\n- **\"bash already bash\".** Outdated: JS now picks `$SHELL`.\n- **HTML script/style skipping.** Rust only handles bare tags; tags with attributes leak their content.\n- **\"replaceAll literal\".** Correct.\n\n## 3. CLI and JSON I/O (`js/src/index.js`, `js/src/cli/**`, `js/src/config/config.ts` ↔ `rust/src/cli.rs`)\n- **Options only in JS.**\n  - `--read-only` and `--disable-tools` (`cli/run-options.js` L216-226).\n  - Subcommands `mcp`, `auth`, `models`, `agent`, `export`, `stats` (index.js L655-661, `cli/cmd/*`).\n  - The middleware mapping `--output-format` to `json-standard` (run-options.js L144-159).\n- **Options only in Rust.** `--working-directory`.\n- **Accepted but no-op in Rust.** `--json-standard claude`, `--input-format`, and `InputMessage.tools`.\n- **Execution.** The Rust CLI **never executes tools or calls a model**. `run_with_input` prints \"Agent (Rust) ready…\" text and finishes with `step_finish{reason:\"stop\"}`.\n- **Env vars read by JS only** (`config/config.ts`, plus `.lenv` via lino-arguments): every `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` variable for\n  - VERBOSE, DRY_RUN, GENERATE_TITLE, OUTPUT_RESPONSE_MODEL, SUMMARIZE_SESSION, COMPACT_JSON\n  - CONFIG, CONFIG_DIR, CONFIG_CONTENT\n  - DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE, DISABLE_PRUNE, ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_MODELS, DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT, EXPERIMENTAL, EXPERIMENTAL_WATCHER\n  - RETRY_TIMEOUT, MAX_RETRY_DELAY, MIN_RETRY_INTERVAL, STREAM_CHUNK/STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, MCP_DEFAULT/MAX_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT\n  - VERIFY_IMAGES_AT_READ_TOOL, **READ_ONLY**, **DISABLE_TOOLS**\n- **Env vars read by Rust.** Only DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_COMPACTION_MODEL(S), DEFAULT_COMPACTION_SAFETY_MARGIN_PERCENT (`defaults.rs`), and PERMISSION_MODE / PERMISSION (`permission.rs` L35-65).\n- **Events emitted by JS.** status, step_start, text, tool_use, tool_result, step_finish, error, input, init, config, idle, session_idle, log, message, permission_request, result, warning.\n  - Envelopes carry `{type, timestamp, sessionID, part}` (`cli/event-handler.js` L57-145). Resume `status` events add mode, sessionID, title and forked (`continuous-mode.js` L200-230).\n- **Events emitted by Rust** (`OutputEvent`, cli.rs L271-315):\n  - status, step_start, text, step_finish, error, plus tool_use, which is defined but never emitted.\n  - `error` is `{timestamp, sessionID:null, error{name,data}}`, and step parts are synthetic.\n\n## 4. Utilities\n- **binary.** These are unrelated modules that share a name.\n  - JS `util/binary.ts` provides `Binary.search/insert` over sorted arrays, which has no Rust counterpart.\n  - Rust `util/binary.rs` holds binary/image detection, ported from read.ts `isBinaryFile` (L481-542), `isImageFile` (L365-390) and `validateImageFormat` (L401-452). The port is equivalent.\n- **filesystem.**\n  - **BUG:** Rust `contains` (`util/filesystem.rs` L52-65) canonicalises, which follows symlinks. When a path does not exist it falls back to a **string prefix**, so `contains(\"/a/b\",\"/a/bc\")` returns true. JS `util/filesystem.ts` uses a lexical `relative()`, which returns false.\n  - Rust `overlaps` is component-based; JS uses string `startsWith('..')`.\n  - Rust lacks `up`/`globUp` (JS L29-72).\n  - The Rust `Filesystem` module is unused.\n- **id.**\n  - Same format and algorithm, and Rust adds `Prefix::Call`.\n  - Rust panics where JS throws; for example, given `\"\"` JS generates a new id while Rust panics.\n  - Rust's counter does a non-atomic load-then-store.\n  - JS `randomBase62` is modulo-biased (`byte%62`); Rust is uniform.\n  - Rust has no zod `schema()`.\n- **permission.**\n  - Ported faithfully: modePolicy, readonlyBash (identical list), parseOverride, policy, wildcard, allStructured, evaluateBash.\n  - Differences: Rust `parse_action_value` rejects non-strings with different text, and Rust has no ask/respond/RejectedError/checkBashTokens.\n  - **Latent panic:** Rust `split_segments` slices `&command[i..i+2]` on byte indices (`permission.rs` L514), which panics on non-ASCII input such as `echo é && ls`.\n  - **Not wired:** no Rust tool consults the policy (X5).\n\n## 5. JS subsystems with no Rust counterpart\n- **agent**: agent definitions and system prompts.\n- **auth**: provider credentials and OAuth.\n- **bus**: event bus for session, part and permission events.\n- **command**: slash or user commands.\n- **file/time**: FileTime read stamps, read-before-edit assert and the per-file lock.\n- **file/ripgrep**: rg discovery, download and files/search wrapper.\n- **format**: post-edit formatters.\n- **mcp**: MCP client and tool timeouts.\n- **patch**: patch application.\n- **project/instance**: worktree and directory context.\n- **provider**: model providers, message sanitising and transforms.\n- **server**: HTTP server and API.\n- **session**: prompt loop, compaction, retry, summary, todo storage and processors.\n- **snapshot**: git snapshots and revert.\n- **storage**: persistent JSON storage.\n- **task tool**: sub-agent tool, absent from the Rust registry.\n- **json-standard claude output**: the Claude-compatible stream format.\n- **cli/cmd subcommands**: mcp, auth, models, agent, export, stats.\n- **continuous-mode / input queue**: stdin streaming and session resume/fork.\n- **verbose-fetch**: HTTP logging.\n- **config via lino-arguments / .lenv**: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env handling.\n- **util/bom**: BOM split/join.\n- **util/read-bounded**: bounded body reading (Rust uses inline equivalents).\n- **util/wildcard**: Rust has it only inside `permission.rs`.\n- **Binary.search/insert**: sorted-array helpers.\n- **Read-only / disable-tools tool filtering**: removes denied tools before a run.\n\n## 6. Prioritised fix list\n1. **grep.** Accept JS `include` (alias to `glob`), default to content output in the JS format (\"Found N matches\", grouped by file, mtime sort, 100 limit, \"No files found\"), and set metadata `{matches,truncated}`. Either use rg or the `ignore` crate (.gitignore, no symlink following), and error on a missing path. `grep.rs` L33-63, L200-330 ↔ `grep.ts` L17-140.\n2. **glob.** Use the `ignore`/`globset` crates with rg semantics (a slash-less pattern matches at any depth, braces, .gitignore, exclude `.git`, no follow). Print absolute paths and \"No files found\", and take the first 100 before sorting. `glob.rs` L69-120 ↔ `glob.ts` L35-62, `ripgrep.ts` L220-240.\n3. **todo.** Align the schema: add `cancelled`, `priority` and `id`; make `activeForm` optional or drop it; use the description from `todowrite.txt`. `todo.rs` L19-39 ↔ `session/todo.ts` L6-19.\n4. **batch.** Collect every call and then `split_off(MAX)`. `batch.rs` L118-128 ↔ `batch.ts` L39-40, L145-166. Consider parallel execution.\n5. **Permissions and FileTime in Rust tools.** Call `permission.rs` from edit, write, bash and webfetch, and add a FileTime equivalent (read stamp, assert before edit, lock), or document the gap. `edit.rs`, `write.rs` ↔ `edit.ts` L69-106, `write.ts` L30-53.\n6. **bash.**\n   - Set the default timeout to 60 000 ms.\n   - Set stdin to null.\n   - Use the `$SHELL` selection (excluding fish and nu).\n   - Interleave stdout and stderr.\n   - Use metadata keys `{output, exit, signal, timedOut, aborted, description}` and the JS timeout text.\n   - Kill the process tree.\n\n   `bash.rs` L18, L98-175, L253-268 ↔ `bash.ts` L21, L47-63, L236-301, L370-390.\n7. **read.** Make an empty file count as 1 line, use JS line splitting (`/\\r?\\n/`, pop the trailing empty line), strip the BOM, apply NFC in canonical_name, and accept numeric strings. `read.rs` L115-177, L346-354 ↔ `read.ts` L23-38, L261-276.\n8. **edit.**\n   - Use the \"File X not found\" and \"Path is a directory\" messages.\n   - Add BOM split/join.\n   - Keep the original endings in filediff.\n   - Produce a unified diff with `@@` headers.\n   - BlockAnchor should pick the best candidate.\n   - Apply the disproportionate-match check to all replacers and throw on it.\n   - Check uniqueness for fuzzy matches.\n\n   `edit.rs` L82-546 ↔ `edit.ts` L19-154, L250-713.\n9. **list.** Use glob-based prefix ignores, respect .gitignore, treat user ignore entries as globs, drop the extra truncation note, and use the JS error texts. `list.rs` L17-41, L111-123, L193-252 ↔ `ls.ts` L8-33, L119.\n10. **webfetch.** Fix script/style skipping when the tag has attributes. Port Turndown-like markdown or use `html2md`. Use the JS status text (\"404\") and timeout text, and add `text/markdown;q=0.7`. Make the tag removal safe for non-ASCII. `webfetch.rs` L157, L196-335 ↔ `webfetch.ts` L60-220.\n11. **CLI.** Add `--read-only`, `--disable-tools` and the `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_READ_ONLY/DISABLE_TOOLS` env vars (a registry filter); add the `timestamp/sessionID/part` envelope; or document that the Rust CLI is a non-executing stub. `cli.rs` L243-470 ↔ `run-options.js` L144-226, `event-handler.js` L57-145.\n12. **Latent panics and bugs.** Fix the `split_segments` byte-index slicing (`permission.rs` L514) and the `Filesystem::contains` string-prefix fallback (`util/filesystem.rs` L59-64) vs `filesystem.ts` `contains`. The id panic on `\"\"` should fall back to generating a new id.\n13. **Minor.**\n    - websearch: `numResults` 0 should become 8; validate the enums; use the JS status text; port the description.\n    - codesearch: validate `tokensNum` rather than clamping.\n    - multiedit: handle `edits: []` in JS.\n14. **Docs.** `rust/README.md` claims 7 tools, but all of them exist. Correct the \"n/a\" rows in `docs/case-studies/issue-335/README.md` §4-§5 as described in §2.",
