[2026-11-02T23:36:27.436Z] [INFO]         "content": "  122 experiments/issue-335/audit/backward-compat-audit.md\n  276 experiments/issue-335/audit/js-rust-parity-audit.md\n  264 experiments/issue-335/audit/memory-leak-audit.md\n  662 total\n# Memory and resource leak audit (issue #335)\n\nScope: `js/src` (primary, long-running CLI / continuous / server modes) and\n`rust/src` (tools + CLI). Read-only audit; no source file was edited.\nBun 1.4.4. Every finding below was checked against the surrounding code.\n\nSeverity: high = grows per tool call / LLM step in normal use; medium = per\nsession or per turn; low = bounded or one-off.\n\nExperiments (all in this directory; run from `js/` with\n`timeout 90 bun ../experiments/issue-335/audit/<file>.ts`):\n\n| Script | Result |\n| --- | --- |\n| `sse-usage-growth.ts` | 1000 simulated steps -> 1000 retained entries; one `consumeLatestUsage()` removes 1 (999 left). CONFIRMED |\n| `tee-no-cancel.ts` | 25 MB streamed response: peak extra RSS 25 MB when the usage branch only `break`s, 7 MB when it also cancels. CONFIRMED |\n| `abort-any-retention.ts` | `AbortSignal.any([longLived, ...])` + abort listener: 0/200 listener closures collected while the parent lives (200/200 without a listener, 200/200 once the timeout source fires). CONFIRMED |\n\n---\n\n## Confirmed\n\n### 1. `SSEUsageExtractor.pendingUsage` grows by one entry per LLM request (high)\n\n- Where: `js/src/util/sse-usage-extractor.ts:15` (`const pendingUsage = new Map()`).\n  Entries are added in `processStreamForUsage` (`:86`). The callers are\n  `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1212` (non-verbose path) and `:1390` (verbose path).\n- Resource: one `SSEUsageData` per streamed response that carries a usage\n  chunk. Small entries, but a module-level map that is never pruned.\n- Growth trigger: every LLM step whose SSE body carries usage. The only consumer\n  is `js/src/session/processor.ts:483` (`consumeLatestUsage()`). It runs only\n  when the AI SDK reported zero tokens, so with a normal provider nothing is\n  ever removed. Even when it does run, it removes only the newest entry.\n- Side effect (correctness): when the SDK does report 0 tokens,\n  `consumeLatestUsage` picks the newest entry across all sessions and requests.\n  With concurrent sessions in server mode, it can pick up another request's\n  usage.\n- Fix: return the request id with the response (or keep a per-request\n  callback) and `consumeUsage(id)` at finish-step. Minimal option: keep only\n  the latest entry (`pendingUsage.clear()` before `set`), or cap the map to the\n  last ~16 entries.\n\n### 2. Usage tee branch is abandoned without `cancel()` (medium: per-response duplication, released at stream end)\n\n- Where: `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1199-1216` (non-verbose path, the default).\n  ```ts\n  const [sdkStream, usageStream] = response.body.tee();\n  ... if (body.length > 50000) break;   // reader never cancelled\n  ```\n- Resource: the tee keeps queueing every later chunk into the unread\n  `usageStream` branch until the response ends. Peak memory for every LLM\n  response over 50 KB is therefore 2x the response size; the experiment\n  measured 25 MB extra for a 25 MB stream versus 7 MB with cancel.\n- Second effect: a tee source is cancelled only when *both* branches cancel.\n  If the SDK cancels its branch without aborting the fetch (for example it\n  stops consuming early), the HTTP body keeps downloading into the orphaned\n  branch.\n- Functional bug in the same spot: usage is normally in the last SSE chunk.\n  Cutting at the first 50 KB means long responses never yield usage, so the\n  #249 fallback silently fails for them.\n- Fix: after the loop, call `reader.cancel().catch(() => {})`. Do not\n  `await` it inline: by the Streams spec a tee branch's cancel promise settles\n  only when the other branch also cancels or the source closes. The first\n  version of the experiment deadlocked on exactly this. Better still, keep\n  reading to the end but retain only a rolling tail (for example the last 8 KB)\n  and parse usage from that.\n\n### 3. bash tool: command-stream keeps the whole output in memory, and the runner is pinned by an abort listener (high for large outputs)\n\n- Where: `js/src/tool/bash.ts:231-232` and `:296-300`.\n  ```ts\n  const timeoutSignal = [REDACTED];           // 60 s default, 10 min max\n  const cancel = AbortSignal.any([ctx.abort, timeoutSignal]);\n  new ProcessRunner(..., { signal: [REDACTED]\n  ```\n- Resource, part (a): unbounded buffering. `capture: true` makes\n  command-stream push every stdout and stderr chunk into\n  `runner.outChunks/errChunks`. See command-stream 2.6.0\n  `src/$.process-runner-execution.mjs:291,331`. At exit it also builds\n  `Buffer.concat(...).toString()` (`:461-468`).\n\n  bash.ts carefully keeps only `2 * MAX_BYTES` of output (`:234-249`), but the\n  runner holds the full output twice. A command that prints 500 MB costs about\n  1 GB. bash.ts only reads `command.result.child.signalCode` from the result.\n- Resource, part (b): retention. `setupExternalAbortSignal` (`:545`) adds\n  `signal.addEventListener('abort', () => stopForAbort(runner))` and never\n  removes it. Bun keeps an `AbortSignal.any` dependent that has a listener\n  alive while a source is alive; the `abort-any-retention.ts` experiment showed\n  0/200 closures collected.\n\n  So the runner and its captured buffers outlive the tool call until the\n  timeout fires (60 s to 10 min) or the turn ends. `prompt.ts` aborts the\n  per-loop controller in `cancel()` via `defer`. In a busy turn, every bash call\n  of the last 60 s or more stays resident at once.\n- Growth trigger: every bash tool call (default timeout 60 s).\n- Fix: pass `capture: false`. The tool consumes `command.stream()` chunks\n  itself. Confirm that the `stream()` and `result.child` paths still work with\n  capture off in the pinned version. Also give the runner its own\n  `AbortController`, link it with a listener that bash.ts removes in a\n  `finally`, and abort the private controller in the `finally` so command-stream's\n  listener is released immediately.\n- Version note: `bun.lock` pins command-stream 2.4.0. Only 2.6.0 is in the\n  local Bun cache, so the line numbers above are from 2.6.0. Re-check 2.4.0\n  when node_modules is installed.\n\n---\n\n## Verified by reading (not reproduced)\n\n### 4. grep tool reads all of rg's output, parses and stats every match, then keeps 100 (medium)\n\n- `js/src/tool/grep.ts:81-83`: `new Response(proc.stdout).text()` buffers the\n  complete `rg --json` output. A broad pattern in a large repo can produce\n  hundreds of MB.\n- `:119-153`: every match is JSON-parsed and `stat`ed one at a time, but only\n  100 are returned (`:157`). The match lines themselves are not truncated\n  until formatting.\n- `:69-77`: the same `AbortSignal.timeout(30 s)` + `any([ctx.abort, ...])`\n  pattern, passed to `Bun.spawn({ signal })`. This may pin the subprocess\n  object for up to 30 s; low.\n- Fix: stream stdout line by line and stop (kill rg) after N matches. Or pass\n  `--max-count`/`--max-columns 2000 --max-columns-preview` and cap the bytes\n  read, as `Ripgrep.files()` already does in `js/src/file/ripgrep.ts`.\n\n### 5. `FileTime.state().read` is never pruned per session (medium)\n\n- `js/src/file/time.ts:21-31,66-67`: `read[sessionID][path] = stamp`.\n- Trigger: every distinct file read or written in every session, including\n  subagent (task) sessions. It is freed only on `Instance.dispose`. In server\n  mode or a long continuous run with many sessions this grows without bound.\n  The per-entry size is small.\n- Fix: delete `read[sessionID]` when a session is deleted or archived, and for\n  subagent sessions when the task tool finishes. Alternatively, cap the number\n  of sessions kept (LRU).\n\n### 6. Continuous mode: per-message idle subscription leaks if `session.idle` never fires (low)\n\n- `js/src/cli/continuous-mode.js:360-369` and `:586-595`: `checkIdle =\n  Bus.subscribeAll(...)`, removed only inside the idle handler.\n- `SessionPrompt.prompt` (`js/src/session/prompt.ts:252-263`) can throw before\n  `loop()` runs: `Session.get`, `SessionRevert.cleanup` or `createUserMessage`.\n  No idle event is published on that path. The subscription then stays forever,\n  and `await messagePromise` hangs the input queue, because `isProcessing` is\n  never reset.\n- Fix: unsubscribe and resolve in the `.catch` of the prompt promise as well,\n  for example with `Promise.race([messagePromise, promptPromise])` plus a\n  `finally(checkIdle)`.\n\n### 7. Upstream retry paths drop error responses without cancelling the body (low)\n\n- `js/src/provider/retry-fetch.ts:463` (5xx retry) and `:556` (429 retry). The\n  `Response` from the failed attempt is discarded and its body is neither read\n  nor cancelled. The connection and buffer are released only by GC. Bodies\n  are usually small.\n- Fix: `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => {})` before\n  `sleep(...)`/`continue`.\n\n### 8. `SessionRetry.sleep` leaves its abort listener attached after the delay elapses (low)\n\n- `js/src/session/retry.ts:130-143`. Called from\n  `js/src/session/processor.ts:805` with the turn's abort signal. Each retry\n  adds a listener (`{ once: true }` only removes it after abort). The listeners\n  are bounded by the retry count and released when the turn ends.\n- Fix: `setTimeout(() => { signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort); resolve(); }, ...)`.\n  `retry-fetch.ts:179-216` already does this correctly.\n\n### 9. `withTimeout` keeps the timer when the wrapped promise rejects (low)\n\n- `js/src/util/timeout.ts:4-7`. `clearTimeout` runs only on fulfilment, so a\n  rejected MCP call (`js/src/mcp/index.ts:610-620`) leaves an unref'd timer\n  and its closure alive until the timeout.\n- Fix: use `promise.finally(() => clearTimeout(timeout))`.\n\n### 10. `Instance.dispose()` leaves the directory in `cache` (low)\n\n- `js/src/project/instance.ts:13,58-62`. `dispose()` disposes the state but does\n  not `cache.delete(directory)`, so the resolved `Context` stays. Only\n  `disposeAll()` clears it (`:73`). One entry per directory ever served\n  (server mode with per-request `directory`).\n- Fix: `cache.delete(Instance.directory)` in `dispose()`.\n\n### 11. Pending permission asks are not dropped on session abort (low)\n\n- `js/src/permission/index.ts:383-390`. `pending[sessionID][id]` holds a\n  promise and its resolve and reject functions until answered or until\n  `Instance` is disposed (`:320-330`). Read-only audit; no source file was edited.\nBun 1.4.4. Every finding below was checked against the surrounding code.\n\nSeverity: high = grows per tool call / LLM step in normal use; medium = per\nsession or per turn; low = bounded or one-off.\n\nExperiments (all in this directory; run from `js/` with\n`timeout 90 bun ../experiments/issue-335/audit/<file>.ts`):\n\n| Script | Result |\n| --- | --- |\n| `sse-usage-growth.ts` | 1000 simulated steps -> 1000 retained entries; one `consumeLatestUsage()` removes 1 (999 left). The callers are\n  `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1212` (non-verbose path) and `:1390` (verbose path).\n- Resource: one `SSEUsageData` per streamed response that carries a usage\n  chunk. Small entries, but a module-level map that is never pruned.\n- Growth trigger: every LLM step whose SSE body carries usage. The only consumer\n  is `js/src/session/processor.ts:483` (`consumeLatestUsage()`). It runs only\n  when the AI SDK reported zero tokens, so with a normal provider nothing is\n  ever removed. Even when it does run, it removes only the newest entry.\n- Side effect (correctness): when the SDK does report 0 tokens,\n  `consumeLatestUsage` picks the newest entry across all sessions and requests.\n  With concurrent sessions in server mode, it can pick up another request's\n  usage.\n- Fix: return the request id with the response (or keep a per-request\n  callback) and `consumeUsage(id)` at finish-step. Minimal option: keep only\n  the latest entry (`pendingUsage.clear()` before `set`), or cap the map to the\n  last ~16 entries.\n\n### 2. Usage tee branch is abandoned without `cancel()` (medium: per-response duplication, released at stream end)\n\n- Where: `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1199-1216` (non-verbose path, the default).\n  ```ts\n  const [sdkStream, usageStream] = response.body.tee();\n  ... if (body.length > 50000) break;   // reader never cancelled\n  ```\n- Resource: the tee keeps queueing every later chunk into the unread\n  `usageStream` branch until the response ends. Peak memory for every LLM\n  response over 50 KB is therefore 2x the response size; the experiment\n  measured 25 MB extra for a 25 MB stream versus 7 MB with cancel.\n- Second effect: a tee source is cancelled only when *both* branches cancel.\n  If the SDK cancels its branch without aborting the fetch (for example it\n  stops consuming early), the HTTP body keeps downloading into the orphaned\n  branch.\n- Functional bug in the same spot: usage is normally in the last SSE chunk.\n  Cutting at the first 50 KB means long responses never yield usage, so the\n  #249 fallback silently fails for them.\n- Fix: after the loop, call `reader.cancel().catch(() => {})`. Do not\n  `await` it inline: by the Streams spec a tee branch's cancel promise settles\n  only when the other branch also cancels or the source closes. The first\n  version of the experiment deadlocked on exactly this. Better still, keep\n  reading to the end but retain only a rolling tail (for example the last 8 KB)\n  and parse usage from that.\n\n### 3. bash tool: command-stream keeps the whole output in memory, and the runner is pinned by an abort listener (high for large outputs)\n\n- Where: `js/src/tool/bash.ts:231-232` and `:296-300`.\n  ```ts\n  const timeoutSignal = [REDACTED];           // 60 s default, 10 min max\n  const cancel = AbortSignal.any([ctx.abort, timeoutSignal]);\n  new ProcessRunner(..., { signal: [REDACTED]\n  ```\n- Resource, part (a): unbounded buffering. `capture: true` makes\n  command-stream push every stdout and stderr chunk into\n  `runner.outChunks/errChunks`. The only consumer\n31:  is `js/src/session/processor.ts:483` (`consumeLatestUsage()`). It runs only\n32:  when the AI SDK reported zero tokens, so with a normal provider nothing is\n33:  ever removed. Usage tee branch is abandoned without `cancel()` (medium: per-response duplication, released at stream end)\n44:\n45:- Where: `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1199-1216` (non-verbose path, the default).\n46:  ```ts\n47:  const [sdkStream, usageStream] = response.body.tee();\n48:  ... if (body.length > 50000) break;   // reader never cancelled\n49:  ```\n50:- Resource: the tee keeps queueing every later chunk into the unread\n51:  `usageStream` branch until the response ends. Peak memory for every LLM\n52:  response over 50 KB is therefore 2x the response size; the experiment\n53:  measured 25 MB extra for a 25 MB stream versus 7 MB with cancel.\n54:- Second effect: a tee source is cancelled only when *both* branches cancel.\n55:  If the SDK cancels its branch without aborting the fetch (for example it\n56:  stops consuming early), the HTTP body keeps downloading into the orphaned\n57:  branch.\n58:- Functional bug in the same spot: usage is normally in the last SSE chunk.\n59:  Cutting at the first 50 KB means long responses never yield usage, so the\n60:  #249 fallback silently fails for them.\n61:- Fix: after the loop, call `reader.cancel().catch(() => {})`. Each\nchange that a script or a model could notice has an option that restores the\nprevious behaviour. Every option is a CLI flag and a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*`\nenv var (`js/src/config/config.ts`, `COMPAT_DEFAULTS`).\n\n| Change                                                               | Option to restore the previous behaviour                        |\n| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| bash runs in `$SHELL` (if POSIX) or bash instead of `/bin/sh`        | `--bash-shell legacy` (or a shell path)                         |\n| bash keeps the tail of long output; edit/write return a confirmation | `--legacy-tool-output`                                          |\n| read past the end of a file is an error                              | `--legacy-tool-output`                                          |\n| edit rejects loose fuzzy matches and an empty `oldString` on a file  | `--legacy-edit-matching`                                        |\n| glob/ls do not follow symlinked directories                          | `--glob-follow-symlinks`                                        |\n| grep searches hidden files; grep times out after 30 s                | `--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0`                       |\n| read returns at most 2000 lines / 50 KB                              | `--read-max-lines 0`, `--read-max-bytes 0`                      |\n| context overflow is `ContextOverflowError` in JSON output            | `--legacy-error-names` (reported as non-retryable `APIError`)   |\n| `tokens.output` excludes reasoning tokens                            | `--legacy-token-usage`                                          |\n| a `stop` finish after tool calls continues the loop                  | `--legacy-loop-exit`                                            |\n| MCP connect is bounded (30 s)                                        | `--mcp-connect-timeout 0`, or `connect_timeout` per server      |\n\nMCP `timeout` keeps its previous meaning (listing tools). A first version of\nthis PR also used it to bound connect, which broke slow servers configured\nwith a short listing timeout, so connect got its own `connect_timeout`.\n\nTests: `js/tests/compat-flags.ts` runs every option with its default and its\nlegacy value, and checks the env-var wiring in a child process.\n\n### 11.2 Memory and resource leaks\n\n| #   | Leak (before)                                                                         | Fix                                                                                    |\n| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| 1   | SSE usage map grew by one entry per request                                           | Bounded to 64 entries, oldest evicted first                                            |\n| 2   | The usage tee branch stopped reading after 50 000 chars, so the tee buffered the rest | Read to the end with a line tracker; only the unfinished line is kept                  |\n| 3   | bash kept the whole output and was pinned by an abort listener on the turn signal    | Own `AbortController`, `capture: false`, bounded tail buffer                           |\n| 4   | grep buffered all rg output and stat-ed every match                                   | Streams rg output, one stat per file, stops after 10 000 matches                       |\n| 5   | FileTime read stamps stayed after a session was deleted                               | `FileTime.clear()` on `Session.remove`                                                 |\n| 6   | Continuous/single-shot mode waited forever for `session.idle` if a prompt failed early | Wait for the prompt (or the HTTP request) to settle, then drop the idle subscription   |\n| 7   | Retried 5xx/429 responses were dropped without cancelling the body                    | `response.body.cancel()` before retrying                                               |\n| 8   | Retry `sleep` left its abort listener on the turn signal                              | Listener removed when the delay elapses                                                |\n| 9   | `withTimeout` kept its timer when the promise rejected                                | `finally(clearTimeout)`                                                                |\n| 10  | `Instance.dispose()` left the directory in the cache                                  | Removed from the cache                                                                 |\n| 11  | Pending permission asks of a cancelled turn stayed until the instance was disposed   | `Permission.clearSession()` on cancel rejects them                                     |\n\nLeft unchanged on purpose:\n\n- A client that disconnects from the HTTP server does not cancel the turn.\n  Clients that POST, disconnect and later poll the session rely on the turn\n  finishing.\n- The optional per-request provider timeout signal is [REDACTED]\n  Clearing it would change the timeout semantics, and it holds no buffers.\n\nTests: the leak regressions in `js/tests/compat-flags.ts`, plus\n`js/tests/sse-usage-extractor.ts`, `js/tests/bash-web-reliability.ts` and\n`js/tests/read-search-reliability-search.ts`.\n\"\"\"\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncd js && npx prettier --write ../docs/case-studies/issue-335/README.md >/dev/null && tail -5 `js/tests/compat-flags.ts` runs every option with its default and its\nlegacy value, and checks the env-var wiring in a child process.\n\n### 11.2 Memory and resource leaks\n\n| #   | Leak (before)                                                                         | Fix                                                                                    |\n| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| 1   | SSE usage map grew by one entry per request                                           | Bounded to 64 entries, oldest evicted first                                            |\n| 2   | The usage tee branch stopped reading after 50 000 chars, so the tee buffered the rest | Read to the end with a line tracker; only the unfinished line is kept                  |\n| 3   | bash kept the whole output and was pinned by an abort listener on the turn signal    | Own `AbortController`, `capture: false`, bounded tail buffer                           |\n| 4   | grep buffered all rg output and stat-ed every match                                   | Streams rg output, one stat per file, stops after 10 000 matches                       |\n| 5   | FileTime read stamps stayed after a session was deleted                               | `FileTime.clear()` on `Session.remove`                                                 |\n| 6   | Continuous/single-shot mode waited forever for `session.idle` if a prompt failed early | Wait for the prompt (or the HTTP request) to settle, then drop the idle subscription   |\n| 7   | Retried 5xx/429 responses were dropped without cancelling the body                    | `response.body.cancel()` before retrying                                               |\n| 8   | Retry `sleep` left its abort listener on the turn signal                              | Listener removed when the delay elapses                                                |\n| 9   | `withTimeout` kept its timer when the promise rejected                                | `finally(clearTimeout)`                                                                |\n| 10  | `Instance.dispose()` left the directory in the cache                                  | Removed from the cache                                                                 |\n| 11  | Pending permission asks of a cancelled turn stayed until the instance was disposed   | `Permission.clearSession()` on cancel rejects them                                     |\n\nLeft unchanged on purpose:\n\n- A client that disconnects from the HTTP server does not cancel the turn.\n  Clients that POST, disconnect and later poll the session rely on the turn\n  finishing.\n- The optional per-request provider timeout signal is [REDACTED]\n  Clearing it would change the timeout semantics, and it holds no buffers.\n\nTests: the leak regressions in `js/tests/compat-flags.ts`, plus\n`js/tests/sse-usage-extractor.ts`, `js/tests/bash-web-reliability.ts`      \"oldString not found in content\",\n342\t        ))\n343\t    }\n344\t}\n345\t\n346\t/// Try exact string replacement\n347\tpub fn try_exact_replace(content: &str, old: &str, new: &str, replace_all: bool) -> Option<String> {\n348\t    if !content.contains(old) {\n349\t        return None;\n350\t    }\n351\t\n352\t    if replace_all {\n353\t        return Some(content.replace(old, new));\n354\t    }\n355\t\n356\t    // Check for unique match\n357\t    let first_idx = content.find(old)?;\n358\t    let last_idx = content.rfind(old)?;\n359\t\n360\t    if first_idx != last_idx  new,\n369\t        &content[first_idx + old.len()..]\n370\t    ))\n371\t}\n372\t\n373\t/// Try line-trimmed matching (ignore leading/trailing whitespace per line)\n374\tpub fn try_line_trimmed_replace(\n375\t    content: &str,\n376\t    old: &str,\n377\t    new: &str,\n378\t    replace_all: bool,\n379\t) -> Option<String> {\n380\t    let content_lines: Vec<&str> =    Some(result)\n424\t}\n425\t\n426\t/// Try whitespace-normalized matching\n427\tpub fn try_whitespace_normalized_replace(\n428\t    content: &str,\n429\t    old: &str,\n430\t    new: &str,\n431\t                if block.len().abs_diff(search_size) <= max_line_delta\n501\t                    && middle_similarity(block, &search_lines) >= BLOCK_ANCHOR_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD\n502\t                {\n503\t                    let matched: String = block.join(\"\\n\");\n504\t                    if !is_disproportionate_match(&matched, old) {\n505\t                        matches.push(matched);\n506\t                    }\n507\t                }\n508\t                break;\n509\t            }\n510\t        }\n511\t    }\n512\t\n513\t    if matches.is_empty() {\n514\t = std::cmp::min(block.len(), search.len()).saturating_sub(2);\n535\t    if lines_to_check == 0 {\n536\t        return 1.0;\n537\t    }\n538\t    let mut similarity = 0.0;\n539\t    for k in 1..=lines_to_check {\n540\t        let a: Vec<char> = block[k].trim().chars().collect();\n541\t        let b: Vec<char> = search[k].trim().chars().collect();\n542\t        let max_len = std::cmp::max(a.len(), b.len());\n543\t        if max_len == 0 {\n544\t            similarity += 1.0 / lines_to_check as f64;\n545\t            continue;\n546\t        }\n547\t        similarity += (1.0 - levenshtein(&a, &b) as f64 / max_len as f64) / lines_to_check as f64;\n548\t    }\n549\t    similarity\n550\t}\n551\t\n552\tfn levenshtein(a: &[char], b: &[char]) -> usize {\n553\t    let mut std::mem::swap(&mut prev, &mut cur);\n562\t    }\n563\t    prev[b.len()]\n564\t}\n565\t\n566\t/// A fuzzy match spanning far more text than oldString (upstream #30932).\n567\tfn >= std::cmp::max(old_lines + 3, old_lines * 2) {\n571\t        return true;\n572\t    }\n573\t    if old_lines == 1 {\n574\t        return false;\n575\t    }\n576\t    let old_len = bool,\n587\t) -> Option<String> {\n588\t    fn remove_indentation(text: &str) -> String {\n589\t        let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();\n590\t        let non_empty: Vec<&&str> = trimmed.slice(1, -1)\n      : trimmed;\n  // Split on whitespace and filter empty strings\n  return inner.split(/\\s+/).filter((s) => s.length > 0);\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve a single compaction model entry (short name, provider/model, or \"same\").\n * @returns {{ providerID: string, modelID: string, useSameModel: boolean }}\n */\nasync function resolveCompactionModelEntry(\n  modelArg,\n  baseProviderID,\n  baseModelID\n) {\n  const useSameModel = modelArg.toLowerCase() === 'same';\n\n  if (useSameModel) {\n    return {\n      providerID: baseProviderID,\n      modelID: baseModelID,\n      useSameModel: true,\n    };\n  }\n\n  if (modelArg.includes('/')) {\n    const parts = modelArg.split('/');\n    return {\n      providerID: parts[0],\n      modelID: parts.slice(1).join('/'),\n      useSameModel: false,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Short name resolution\n  const { Provider } = await import('../provider/provider.ts');\n  const resolved = await Provider.resolveShortModelName(modelArg);\n  if (!resolved) {\n    throw new Error('ProviderModelNotFoundError');\n  }\n  return {\n    providerID: resolved.providerID,\n    modelID: resolved.modelID,\n    useSameModel: false,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve a built-in cascade entry against the run's own provider only.\n *\n * The built-in cascade is narrowed to the configured provider anyway (#307),\n * so resolving its short names across the whole provider registry only to\n * drop the result afterwards was wasted work — and it logged records such as\n * `{\"providerID\":\"opencode\",\"message\":\"resolved short model name\"}` that a\n * host reads as the run using OpenCode (#313). Only the base provider's own\n * catalog is consulted here; any other provider is never looked up.\n *\n * @returns {Promise<{providerID: string, modelID: string, useSameModel: boolean} | null>}\n *   the entry, or `null` when the base provider does not serve it\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/313\n */\nasync function resolveEntryWithinProvider(\n  modelArg,\n  baseProviderID,\n  baseModelID\n) {\n  if (modelArg.toLowerCase() === 'same') {\n    return {\n      providerID: baseProviderID,\n      modelID: baseModelID,\n      useSameModel: true,\n    };\n  }\n\n  if (modelArg.includes('/')) {\n    const parts = modelArg.split('/');\n    if (parts[0] !== baseProviderID) {\n      return null;\n    }\n    return {\n      providerID: parts[0],\n      modelID: parts.slice(1).join('/'),\n      useSameModel: false,\n    };\n  }\n\n  const { Provider } = await import('../provider/provider.ts');\n  if (!(await Provider.hasModel(baseProviderID, modelArg))) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  return { providerID: baseProviderID, modelID: modelArg, useSameModel: false };\n}\n\n/**\n * Narrow a built-in compaction default to the provider the run was pointed at.\n *\n * The shipped cascade names OpenCode models, because the shipped base model is\n * an OpenCode one. A run launched with `--model formalai/formal-ai` inherited\n * that cascade unchanged, so compaction — and the session summary, which reuses\n * the compaction model — called a provider the operator may hold no credentials\n * for. Every one of those calls fails, and the failures read as the run having\n * failed.\n *\n * Only the *built-in* defaults are narrowed, and only for a run pointed away\n * from the built-in default provider. A cascade the operator named\n * (`--compaction-model`, `--compaction-models`, or the\n * `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_DEFAULT_COMPACTION_MODEL*` env vars) is an explicit\n * choice and is left alone, cross-provider or not; and a run on the shipped\n * provider keeps the shipped cascade, whose extra entries are the rate-limit\n * fallbacks it was written for.\n *\n * @param {{providerID: string, modelID: string, useSameModel: boolean}[]} kept\n *   Entries served by the base provider\n * @param {string[]} dropped Default entries, as written, that were left out\n * @param {string} baseProviderID Provider of the model that runs the turns\n * @param {string} baseModelID Model that runs the turns\n * @returns {{providerID: string, modelID: string, useSameModel: boolean}[]}\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/307\n */\nfunction inheritBaseProvider(kept, dropped, baseProviderID, baseModelID) {\n  if (dropped.length === 0) {\n    return kept;\n  }\n\n  const inherited =\n    kept.length > 0\n      ? kept\n      : [\n          {\n            providerID: baseProviderID,\n            modelID: baseModelID,\n            useSameModel: true,\n          },\n        ];\n\n  Log.Default.info(() => ({\n    message: 'default compaction models narrowed to the configured provider',\n    hint: 'Secondary calls (compaction, session summary) inherit --model unless a compaction model is named explicitly',\n    baseProviderID,\n    baseModelID,\n    // The names as written in the default: they were never resolved, so they\n    // say nothing about which provider would have served them (#313).\n    dropped,\n    kept: inherited.map((entry) =>\n      entry.useSameModel ? 'same' : `${entry.providerID}/${entry.modelID}`\n    ),\n  }));\n\n  return inherited;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse compaction model config from argv.\n * Supports both --compaction-model (single) and --compaction-models (cascade).\n * When --compaction-models is specified, it overrides --compaction-model.\n * The special value \"same\" means use the base model for compaction.\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/219\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/232\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/307\n */\nasync function parseCompactionModelConfig(\n  argv,\n  baseProviderID,\n  baseModelID,\n  defaultOptions = {}\n) {\n  const defaultCompactionSafetyMarginPercent =\n    getDefaultCompactionSafetyMarginPercent(defaultOptions);\n\n  // Get safety margin from CLI\n  const cliSafetyMarginArg = getCompactionSafetyMarginFromProcessArgv();\n  const compactionSafetyMarginPercent = cliSafetyMarginArg\n    ? parseInt(cliSafetyMarginArg, 10)\n    : (argv['compaction-safety-margin'] ??\n      defaultCompactionSafetyMarginPercent);\n\n  // Check for --compaction-models (cascade) first — it overrides --compaction-model\n  const cliCompactionModelsArg = getCompactionModelsFromProcessArgv();\n  const defaultCompactionModels = getDefaultCompactionModels(defaultOptions);\n  const compactionModelsSource =\n    cliCompactionModelsArg ||\n    (argv['compaction-models'] &&\n      argv['compaction-models'] !== defaultCompactionModels)\n      ? Utilities\n- **binary.** These are unrelated modules that share a name.\n  - JS `util/binary.ts` provides `Binary.search/insert` over sorted arrays, which has no Rust counterpart.\n  - Rust `util/binary.rs` holds binary/image detection, ported from read.ts `isBinaryFile` (L481-542), `isImageFile` (L365-390) and `validateImageFormat` (L401-452). The port is equivalent.\n- **filesystem.**\n  - **BUG:** Rust `contains` (`util/filesystem.rs` L52-65) canonicalises, which follows symlinks. When a path does not exist it falls back to a **string prefix**, so `contains(\"/a/b\",\"/a/bc\")` returns true. JS `util/filesystem.ts` uses a lexical `relative()`, which returns false.\n  - Rust `overlaps` is component-based; JS uses string `startsWith('..')`.\n  - Rust lacks `up`/`globUp` (JS L29-72).\n  - The Rust `Filesystem` module is unused.\n- **id.**\n  - Same format and algorithm, and Rust adds `Prefix::Call`.\n  - Rust panics where JS throws; for example, given `\"\"` JS generates a new id while Rust panics.\n  - Rust's counter does a non-atomic load-then-store.\n  - JS `randomBase62` is modulo-biased (`byte%62`); Rust is uniform.\n  - Rust has no zod `schema()`.\n- **permission.**\n  - Ported faithfully: modePolicy, readonlyBash (identical list), parseOverride, policy, wildcard, allStructured, evaluateBash.\n  - Differences: Rust `parse_action_value` rejects non-strings with different text, and Rust has no ask/respond/RejectedError/checkBashTokens.\n  - **Latent panic:** Rust `split_segments` slices `&command[i..i+2]` on byte indices (`permission.rs` L514), which panics on non-ASCII input such as `echo é && ls`.\n  - **Not wired:** no Rust tool consults the policy (X5).\n\n## 5. JS subsystems with no Rust counterpart\n- **agent**: agent definitions and system prompts.\n- **auth**: provider credentials and OAuth.\n- **bus**: event bus for session, part and permission events.\n- **command**: slash or user commands.\n- **file/time**: FileTime read stamps, read-before-edit assert and the per-file lock.\n- **file/ripgrep**: rg discovery, download and files/search wrapper.\n- **format**: post-edit formatters.\n- **mcp**: MCP client and tool timeouts.\n- **patch**: patch application.\n- **project/instance**: worktree and directory context.\n- **provider**: model providers, message sanitising and transforms.\n- **server**: HTTP server and API.\n- **session**: prompt loop, compaction, retry, summary, todo storage and processors.\n- **snapshot**: git snapshots and revert.\n- **storage**: persistent JSON storage.\n- **task tool**: sub-agent tool, absent from the Rust registry.\n- **json-standard claude output**: the Claude-compatible stream format.\n- **cli/cmd subcommands**: mcp, auth, models, agent, export, stats.\n- **continuous-mode / input queue**: stdin streaming and session resume/fork.\n- **verbose-fetch**: HTTP logging.\n- **config via lino-arguments / .lenv**: `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env handling.\n- **util/bom**: BOM split/join.\n- **util/read-bounded**: bounded body reading (Rust uses inline equivalents).\n- **util/wildcard**: Rust has it only inside `permission.rs`.\n- **Binary.search/insert**: sorted-array helpers.\n- **Read-only / disable-tools tool filtering**: removes denied tools before a run.\n\n## 6. Each Rust CLI run is a separate process with no session, and `batch` runs calls one after another, so neither could take effect.\n- **Permissions:** `permission.rs` is still not called by the tools, because the CLI never runs tools for a model.\n- **Cross-cutting differences** from the audit remain: serde defaults versus raw JS args, the `AgentError` wrapper text, and paths joined without `..` normalisation.\n- **edit:** a file that is not valid UTF-8 still fails to read.\n- **multiedit:** `edits: []` returns empty output, where JS throws.\n- **CLI output:** the Rust CLI does not call an LLM and does not emit the JS event envelope.\n\n**Deliberate divergences** (listed in the notes file):\n- **edit:**\n  - Edits run on an LF copy of the file and the original line endings are restored afterwards. Untouched lines of a mixed-ending file keep their bytes.\n  - An empty match candidate is skipped. JS would insert `newString` at the start of the file.\n  - The edit and write descriptions keep the Rust text, because the JS text claims a read-first rule Rust does not enforce.\n- **bash:**\n  - The default timeout stays 2 minutes; JS uses 1.\n  - stdout and stderr are joined with a `--- stderr ---` separator instead of interleaved.\n  - `aborted` is always false.\n- **codesearch:** `tokensNum` is clamped into range instead of rejected.\n- **webfetch:** markdown comes from a small converter, not Turndown.\n- **glob and list:** skip `.git` at any depth.\n- **grep:** checks the whole file for NUL bytes when deciding it is binary.\n- **legacy glob output:** keeps the 100-result limit."

edit/write return a confirmation; read past EOF is an error | `--legacy-tool-output` |\n| edit refuses loose fuzzy matches and an empty `oldString` on an existing file | `--legacy-edit-matching` |\n| glob/ls do not follow symlinked directories | `--glob-follow-symlinks` |\n| grep searches hidden files and stops after 30 s | `--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0` |\n| read returns at most 2000 lines / 50 KB | `--read-max-lines 0`, `--read-max-bytes 0` |\n| context overflow is reported as `ContextOverflowError` | `--legacy-error-names` (non-retryable `APIError`, as before) |\n| `tokens.output` excludes reasoning tokens | `--legacy-token-usage` |\n| a `stop` finish after tool calls continues the loop | `--legacy-loop-exit` |\n| MCP connect is bounded (30 s) | `--mcp-connect-timeout 0` or per-server `connect_timeout` |\n\nMCP `timeout` keeps its old meaning (tools listing); connect got its own `connect_timeout` so that a short listing timeout no longer cuts a slow connect. `js/tests/compat-flags.ts` runs every switch in both states and checks the env wiring in a child process; the Rust switches are tested through `ToolContext::with_settings`.\n\n**Memory and resource leaks fixed (JS):** unbounded SSE usage map; the usage tee branch that stopped reading and made the tee buffer the rest of the stream; bash output and abort-listener retention; grep buffering all rg output; FileTime stamps after a session is deleted; continuous/single-shot mode waiting forever for `session.idle` when a prompt failed early; retried 5xx/429 bodies not cancelled; retry `sleep` abort listener; `withTimeout` timer on rejection; `Instance.dispose()` leaving the cache entry; pending permission asks of a cancelled turn. Each has a regression test. Two items were left on purpose (client disconnect does not cancel a turn; the per-request provider timeout signal) — reasons in §11.2.\n\n**Rust parity.** `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `read`, `edit`, `bash`, `todo`, `batch`, `webfetch`, `websearch` now match the JS tools (output, errors, limits; edit diffs checked against output of the JS code), with the same compatibility switches plus `--read-only` / `--disable-tools`. Latent Rust bugs fixed: non-ASCII panic in `permission.rs`, prefix match in `Filesystem::contains`, panic on an empty id. Not done, with reasons: FileTime and the per-file lock (each Rust CLI run is a separate process with no session), permission checks in tools (the Rust CLI never runs tools for a model), and the absent LLM/session/provider/MCP layers (pre-existing). Divergences are listed in `experiments/issue-335/audit/rust-parity-fixes.md`.\n\n**CI checks that also failed on `main`:** Security (`body-parser` 2.3.0, GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, bumped to 2.4.0); __MODELS__; __DEPS__.\n\"\"\"\nmarker=\"## Deliberate deviations from upstream\"\ns=s.replace(marker, review.strip()+\"\\n\\n\"+marker)\nopen('/tmp/t335/pr-body-new.md','w').write(s)\nEOF\nwc -l /tmp/t335/pr-body-new.md"

retry delays never exceed the `setTimeout` limit; API errors\n  include the body's message.\n- A `retry-after` longer than the retry timeout now stops the turn instead of\n  starting another step, and retry-only errors can be saved on a message.\n- Interrupted tools keep their start time and partial output and are marked\n  `interrupted`; #335\n\n## Summary\n\nThis ports the reliability fixes that upstream [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) made after our fork point (`0068cb305f`, 2025-11-19, up to `d93568f334`) to the tools, session loop, provider layer and MCP client we already have. **No tools were added.** Each fix applies to code we already have, and each has a regression test.\n\nUpstream moved its code twice since the fork (to Effect services, then from `packages/opencode` to `packages/core`), so no upstream commit could be cherry-picked. I listed all 900 upstream `fix` commits that touch tools, session, provider or MCP code (`docs/case-studies/issue-335/data/`), triaged each one as PORT, ALREADY-HAVE or N/A (`analysis/A–D`), and re-implemented the PORT items in JS. Where a defect also exists in the Rust port, it is fixed in Rust too.\n\nFull case study, including the requirements, timeline, method, online research, libraries considered and verification: [`docs/case-studies/issue-335/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-335-cc63abda9307/docs/case-studies/issue-335).\n\n## What changed\n\n### Edit and write (JS + Rust)\n\n| Defect | Upstream | Fix |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Parallel edits of one file lost updates | #4388, #23483 | Per-file lock (`FileTime.withLock`) for `edit` and `write` |\n| Loose fuzzy match could replace unrelated code; empty `oldString` overwrote a file | #30932 | Stricter thresholds, size guard, explicit error |\n| CRLF / mixed endings / UTF-8 BOM not preserved | #9443, #53166, #23797 | Endings and BOM kept; untouched lines never rewritten |\n| `replaceAll` interpreted `$&`, `$1` | — | Literal replacement |\n| False \"modified since read\" (clock comparison, `dir/./a` vs `dir/a`) | #17835, #20367 | `{mtime, size}` stamp, canonical path keys |\n| `edit` right after `write` failed; empty tool output | `66f9bdab32` | `write` records a read; short confirmations |\n\n### Read, grep, glob, ls (JS + Rust)\n\n| Defect | Upstream | Fix |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `glob`/`ls` hung after 100 results (rg blocked on a full pipe) | #10833 | Stream cancelled and rg killed; abort passed through |\n| `grep` dropped all matches when one path was unreadable (rg exit 2) | #8612 | Matches kept, plus a note |\n| `grep` deadlock on large stderr, no cancel, hidden files skipped | #39238, #7501 | Pipes drained together, abort + 30 s timeout, `--hidden` without `.git` |\n| `read` relative to the worktree root, unbounded output, whole file read for the binary check, `\\r` leaked | `6cf2c3e3db`, #14009, #51011 | Session directory, 50 KB cap, 4 KB sample, CRLF split |\n| macOS screenshot names (U+202F, curly quotes) \"not found\" | #45807, #50953 | Unique entry matched after canonicalizing |\n\n### Bash and web tools (JS + Rust)\n\n| Defect | Upstream | Fix |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `bash` ran `/bin/sh` (dash), so bash syntax failed | #3494, #5205 | `$SHELL` if usable, otherwise bash (zsh on macOS) |\n| Long output kept the start and dropped the end, where errors are; UTF-8 split (Rust panic) | #22660, #39403 | Tail kept on character boundaries |\n| `echo x > file` passed an `echo*` allow rule in read-only/plan mode | #6737 | Write redirects checked as a separate `>` command |\n| Rust `bash` deadlocked on full stderr and lost output on timeout | (found here) | Concurrent pipes, partial output, signal reported |\n| Web tools: timeout did not cover the body; 5 MB limit checked only after reading it all; Cloudflare 403; Exa key ignored | #21378, #33259, #10328, #16362 | `AbortSignal.timeout`, bounded streaming reader, one honest retry, shared Exa client |\n| `Tool.define` stacked wrappers on each init; `task` leaked its subscription | #16952, #9992 | Copy before wrap; `try/finally` |\n\n### Session loop, provider transforms, MCP (JS only; Rust has none of these yet)\n\n| Defect | Upstream | Fix |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Context overflow (400 \"prompt is too long\", 413, `context_length_exceeded`) ended the session | #6480, #14707 | `ContextOverflowError` → compact and continue; a second overflow stops with a clear error |\n| Finish `stop` after tool calls ended the loop before the results were sent back | #14973, #26178 | Loop continues while the last step has completed tool calls |\n| Retryable 5xx stream errors, plain-text rate limits, Vertex exhaustion, OpenAI item 404, `ZlibError` not retried | #12768, #10590, #24063, #19104 | Classified as retryable; delays capped at 2³¹−1 ms |\n| `retry-after` beyond the retry timeout: `process()` returned `undefined` and the loop started another step | (found here) | Normal final-error path, turn stops; retry-only errors added to the message error union (saving them threw a `ZodError`) |\n| Lone surrogates, empty Anthropic/Bedrock blocks, empty user messages, foreign signatures/reasoning → 400 | #25934, #4811, `021e42c0bb1`, #21370 | Sanitized per target model |\n| Shallow-spread cache options, wrong Bedrock cache point, Moonshot schema errors | #10323, #11664, #18959, #24730, #11984 | `mergeDeep`, `cachePoint: { type: 'default' }`, schema fixes |\n| Interrupted tools lost their start time; raw string tool input broke Gemini; tool events without `tool-input-start` dropped | #27254, #21709 | `interrupted` marker, `{ value }` wrapping, `ensureToolCall` |\n| Reasoning tokens charged twice; Anthropic thinking budget branch never ran | #21047, (found here) | Charged once; `model.npm` passed |\n| MCP: no connect or `tools/list` timeout, endless pagination, sequential listing, leaked failed clients, silent removal on bad URL, no-tools servers failed, results without `content` dropped, timed-out calls kept running, `_` in server names broke per-tool timeouts, connect timeout was `NaN`, grandchildren left on dispose | #6760, #19200, #31442, #13229, #25019, #31595, #31271, #7879, #32244, #15516 | All fixed; see §6.3 of the case study |\n| `cancel()` rejected queued callers with `undefined` | `6c9b2c37a5` | `AbortError` |\n\n## Review follow-up: compatibility, memory, Rust parity\n\nAnswer to the review comment (\"not break anything previously working … configuration for breaking changes … memory leaks … parity between JavaScript and Rust\"). Details: §11 of the case study and the audits in `experiments/issue-335/audit/`.\n\n**Backward compatibility.** The JSON input format, event types and envelope are unchanged; stored sessions still load. Every change a script or model could notice has a switch that restores the previous behaviour, as a CLI flag and a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env var (JS `src/config/config.ts`, Rust `src/compat.rs`):\n\n| Change | Restore previous behaviour |\n| --- | --- |\n| bash runs `$SHELL` (if POSIX) or bash instead of `/bin/sh` | `--bash-shell legacy` (or a path) |\n| bash keeps the tail of long output; edit/write return a confirmation; read past EOF is an error | `--legacy-tool-output` |\n| edit refuses loose fuzzy matches and an empty `oldString` on an existing file | `--legacy-edit-matching` |\n| glob/ls do not follow symlinked directories | `--glob-follow-symlinks` |\n| grep searches hidden files and stops after 30 s | `--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0` |\n| read returns at most 2000 lines / 50 KB | `--read-max-lines 0`, `--read-max-bytes 0` |\n| context overflow is reported as `ContextOverflowError` | `--legacy-error-names` (non-retryable `APIError`, as before) |\n| `tokens.output` excludes reasoning tokens | `--legacy-token-usage` |\n| a `stop` finish after tool calls continues the loop | `--legacy-loop-exit` |\n| MCP connect is bounded (30 s) | `--mcp-connect-timeout 0` or per-server `connect_timeout` |\n\nMCP `timeout` keeps its old meaning (tools listing); connect got its own `connect_timeout` so that a short listing timeout no longer cuts a slow connect. `js/tests/compat-flags.ts` runs every switch in both states and checks the env wiring in a child process; the Rust switches are tested through `ToolContext::with_settings`.\n\n**Memory and resource leaks fixed (JS):** unbounded SSE usage map; the usage tee branch that stopped reading and made the tee buffer the rest of the stream; bash output and abort-listener retention; grep buffering all rg output; FileTime stamps after a session is deleted; continuous/single-shot mode waiting forever for `session.idle` when a prompt failed early; retried 5xx/429 bodies not cancelled; retry `sleep` abort listener; `withTimeout` timer on rejection; `Instance.dispose()` leaving the cache entry; pending permission asks of a cancelled turn. Each has a regression test. Two items were left on purpose (client disconnect does not cancel a turn; the per-request provider timeout signal) — reasons in §11.2.\n\n**Rust parity.** `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `read`, `edit`, `bash`, `todo`, `batch`, `webfetch`, `websearch` now match the JS tools (output, errors, limits; edit diffs checked against output of the JS code), with the same compatibility switches plus `--read-only` / `--disable-tools`. Latent Rust bugs fixed: non-ASCII panic in `permission.rs`, prefix match in `Filesystem::contains`, panic on an empty id. Not done, with reasons: FileTime and the per-file lock (each Rust CLI run is a separate process with no session), permission checks in tools (the Rust CLI never runs tools for a model), and the absent LLM/session/provider/MCP layers (pre-existing). Divergences are listed in `experiments/issue-335/audit/rust-parity-fixes.md`.\n\n**CI checks that also failed on `main`** (fixed here, no manual step; §11.4 of the case study):\n\n- **Security:** `body-parser` 2.3.0 (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, high), bumped to 2.4.0 in both lockfiles.\n- **Free Model Drift:** Kilo withdrew `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`, the default model and first compaction model in JS and Rust. The defaults are now `kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (cascade `(kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free kilo/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free same)`). For backward compatibility `kilo/nemotron-3-super-free` (and the bare short name) stays accepted as a deprecated alias that runs on Ultra and logs a warning naming the replacement; the drift script skips aliases and checks that their targets are built-ins.\n- **Model Catalogue:** `check-default-models.mjs` reported the same withdrawn default; fixed by the new default. The alias warning lives in `kilo-deprecation.ts` so `kilo.ts` stays dependency-free (this workflow runs without installing packages).\n- **Dependency Freshness:** all direct npm dependencies bumped to latest (AI SDK and `@ai-sdk/*`, MCP SDK, opentui 0.8, `glob` 14, `minimatch` 11, `hono`, `command-stream` 2.6, …; no source changes needed). `solid-js` unpinned (opentui#689 is closed) and the obsolete `seroval` override dropped. `lino-arguments` stays on 0.3.x and is pinned: 0.4.0 makes the agent exit at startup when the host has both `http_proxy` and `HTTP_PROXY` (reported upstream: link-foundation/lino-arguments#50). Rust: `globset`, `ignore`, `similar` and `uuid` updated to their latest patch releases for `cargo outdated`.\n\n**Crash in git worktrees and submodules (found while checking the dependency refresh).** `Project.fromDirectory` wrote its id cache to `.git/opencode` without awaiting or handling the write. In a worktree or submodule `.git` is a file, so the write rejected with `ENOTDIR` and the `unhandledRejection` handler exited the CLI with code 1, on every run. The id is now cached in the common git dir (as upstream does) and a failed write is only logged. Reproduction: `bun experiments/issue-335/project-worktree.ts <worktree dir>`; regression test `js/tests/project-worktree.ts` fails before the fix and passes after.\n\n## Deliberate deviations from upstream\n\n- **No new tools** (requirement of the issue): `apply_patch`, `lsp`, `question`, `skill`, `plan-*` and `code-mode` were not added. The unregistered `patch` and `multiedit` stay unregistered.\n- **`write` keeps \"no restrictions\"**: upstream requires a prior read; the fork removed that on purpose (`db682c8`).\n- **Image formats**: upstream stopped sending SVG/BMP/TIFF/ICO/AVIF as images (#21114). The fork supports them on a maintainer's request (`86f24ac`), so that change was not ported.\n- After an overflow compaction, upstream replays the user message; here the existing flow (summary plus a synthetic \"Continue if you have next steps\") is kept.\n\nKnown remaining limitation: when a model overflows, the compaction model cascade does not move on to the next model; the overflow is reported instead.\n\n## How to reproduce (example: lost parallel edits)\n\n```bash\ngit worktree add /tmp/main origin/main && cp -r experiments/issue-335 /tmp/main/experiments/\nln -s \"$PWD/js/node_modules\" /tmp/main/js/node_modules\n(cd /tmp/main && bun experiments/issue-335/edit-write/01-parallel-edits.ts)\n# runs=20 both-fulfilled-but-one-edit-lost=15 rejected=1\nbun experiments/issue-335/edit-write/01-parallel-edits.ts\n# runs=20 both-fulfilled-but-one-edit-lost=0 rejected=0\n```\n\nOther reproductions are in `experiments/issue-335/{edit-write,read-search,bash-web}/`.\n\n## Tests\n\n- New: `js/tests/edit-write-reliability.ts`, `read-search-reliability-{read,search}.ts`, `bash-web-reliability.ts`, regressions), `project-worktree.ts`; Kilo alias tests in `free-model-catalog.ts` / `model-drift.ts`; Rust `rust/tests/compat.rs` and `rust/tests/tool_{edit,write,read,grep,glob,bash,webfetch,websearch,codesearch}.rs` (plus the parity tests).\n- `cd js && bun test --timeout 30000 ./tests/*.js ./tests/*.ts`: 1150 pass, 4 todo, 0 fail before the review follow-up; the full suite runs in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows for every push.\n- Review follow-up, locally: 10 focused JS files (compat, session, MCP, models, CLI options, AI SDK, project worktree, snapshot) 187 pass, 0 fail; `npm run lint`, `format:check`, `check:file-size` clean; `bun scripts/check-model-drift.mjs` and `node scripts/check-npm-freshness.mjs` exit 0; `npm audit --audit-level=high` clean.\n- `cd rust && cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && cargo test`: clean, 563 pass.\n\nRelease notes:
